articles.title: Marnus Labuschagne dropped! Australia chief selector makes big announcement
articles.summary: Marnus Labuschagne is set to miss Australia's upcoming Test series against New Zealand, with chief selector George Bailey confirming that the out-of-form
articles.body: Marnus Labuschagne is set to miss Australia's upcoming Test series against New Zealand, with chief selector George Bailey confirming that the out-of-form batter will not be considered for the opening Test in December. The decision comes after a prolonged lean patch that has continued through Australia's recent assignments against Bangladesh and South Africa.Although Australia are yet to announce their squad for the first Test, Bailey made it clear that Labuschagne is currently not in their plans for the New Zealand series, which will be played across December and January."At this stage, we won't be considering Marn for selection for certainly that first Test, but for the New Zealand series," Bailey told reporters on Monday.With speculation mounting over the 31-year-old's position in the side, the selection chair said the decision would also give the batter some clarity as he looks to regain form in domestic cricket."There's been a lot of speculation around his place in the team, and so I think this gives him a little bit of space and clears up a bit of conjecture as we work through the next round of [Sheffield] Shield cricket," Bailey added.This is the second time in the last 17 months that Labuschagne has lost his place in Australia's Test plans. Once a regular fixture at No. 3, he has struggled to produce a century, going 49 innings without one since his last Test hundred during the 2023 Ashes in Manchester.His previous dip in form had also cost him his place during Australia's tour of the West Indies following last year's World Test Championship final, although he remained part of the squad.Labuschagne subsequently worked his way back into the playing XI after making a strong start to the domestic season. He returned to his preferred No. 3 position for the home Ashes and began with half-centuries in each of the first two Tests. However, his form faded thereafter, and he has not managed a fifty in his last 16 innings.His struggles were particularly evident in the recent assignments against Bangladesh and South Africa. Labuschagne managed just 36 runs at an average of 12 against Bangladesh before scoring 131 runs at 21.83 in South Africa. Australia failed to win either series, drawing 1-1 against Bangladesh before suffering a 2-1 defeat in South Africa.Bailey keeps door open for Labuschagne's returnDespite confirming that Labuschagne would not be considered for the New Zealand series at this stage, Bailey insisted that the batter's international career was far from over.Australia have a demanding Test schedule ahead, with a five-match tour of India following the four Tests against New Zealand. They are also scheduled to play an away Ashes series next year, leaving Labuschagne with opportunities to force his way back into contention."It's still possible, absolutely," Bailey said."I think we all know how good and how effective Marnus can be at his best. But that performance hasn't been there. I think he's missed some opportunities, some promising starts in Darwin [against Bangladesh] and even in South Africa as well, to go on and get a big score that we'd like and would have liked for some time, and that just hasn't happened."Bailey also stressed that Australia had not permanently shut the door on the batter."But I don't think we've ever ruled anyone out permanently…and that's no different in this case," he said.Australia's squad for the opening Test against New Zealand will be announced after the next round of Sheffield Shield matches, which gets underway on Wednesday, November 11.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Three net bowlers, camp in Wellington: India chalk out Test preparations
articles.summary: HAMILTON: The Indian cricket team is firming up its preparations for the upcoming two-match Test series against New Zealand.
articles.body: HAMILTON: The Indian cricket team is firming up its preparations for the upcoming two-match Test series against New Zealand. The players in the squad will leave for Wellington from Hamilton and will be assisted by batting coach Sitanshu Kotak and bowling coach Morne Morkel. The players in the India A set-up, in Christchurch, will link up with the group in Wellington.Kotak revealed on Monday that the team management is also considering keeping Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi back for the Test camp, and head coach Gautam Gambhir will soon make the final call. The head coach himself will stay back with the ODI team."Gautam will have to be here, One Day World Cup is coming, so he will be staying here, and probably Sairaj (Bahutule) will stay here. Me, Morne (Morkel) and some other staff will go to Wellington, this is the plan. It will be finalised by Gautam, so it can change. We will just try and see that their (Test squad) loading, their fitness, their practice, they should do enough preparation, as much as the conditions permit us. Arsh (Arshdeep Singh), (Auqib) Nabi, and Gurnoor (Brar), if I am not wrong, will stay back for Tests," said Kotak on Monday.India played the first two ODIs in challenging conditions and Kotak felt while the colour of the ball will change, the experience will hold the Test-bound players in good stead for the two-match series. Both Auckland and Wellington fixtures were low-scoring affairs and batters from both teams found life difficult in conditions which were seaming and swinging, and offered encouraging bounce to the bowlers. With a short turnaround time between the ODI and Test series, the Indian camp is hoping that the Wellington sessions will keep the squad ready for Basin Reserve opener.Additionally, players like Jasprit Bumrah, Ravindra Jadeja, Devdutt Padikkal, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan have been with the India A team and got some crucial game time under their belt."The wicket in both the ODIs had swing and when it stopped after 4-6 overs, there was seam movement and a little awkward bounce also. So, in hindsight, it is a good thing, because in the Test match, the same thing can happen... only the ball will be red. Yes, the intent and mindset will be of One Day in One Day, but one thing is that with the wickets here, thicker grass, 12-14 [mm of grass, and the conditions, you can get an idea. Even if there is more green in the Test pitch, there is not much green in this one. But it is quite a good condition to play... it is challenging."Plus, there are many India A matches which the red ball players are playing. So that is also a big advantage for batters and bowlers because they would know where to bowl, what length to bowl, how much to hit, how much to release, and what help to expect."So all in all, the preparation has been very good and on top of that, the Test players are going for a camp on the 11th, so we will also get 5-6 sessions. Fingers crossed, we should be ready for the Test series as well," explained Kotak.After wrapping up their ODI committments, Shubman Gill and other members of the Test squad will head to Wellington while the remaining team heads to Tauranga for the last two fixtures, where the team will be led by Shreyas Iyer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Coaches are afraid’: Ex-India coach opens up on confronting Virat Kohli over technical flaw
articles.summary: Former India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate has opened up about a behind-the-scenes conversation with Virat Kohli during India's tour of Australia,
articles.body: Former India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate has opened up about a behind-the-scenes conversation with Virat Kohli during India's tour of Australia, revealing how carefully he planned a technical intervention with the batting superstar after noticing a recurring flaw in his batting.Kohli had endured a difficult run during the tour, repeatedly getting dismissed while attempting to drive deliveries outside the off stump. With the same mode of dismissal becoming a talking point, questions were raised about whether the Indian coaching staff was doing enough to address the issue.Speaking on the talkSPORT Cricket podcast, Ten Doeschate explained that approaching an established international star with technical suggestions is not always straightforward. He believes the growing influence of players in modern cricket has made several coaches hesitant about intervening when senior players are going through a difficult phase."I think a lot of coaches are afraid to make interventions because it can be seen that you are, you know, trying to justify your job, or you're interfering, or just saying things for the sake of saying it," Ten Doeschate said."You've got to strike the balance of making an intervention that's going to help the player, or confusing them."The former Netherlands all-rounder said he was determined not to let the fear of how a player might react prevent him from offering advice. He recalled eventually approaching Kohli during the fourth Test of the Australia tour to discuss his repeated dismissals."I never want to be a coach who is scared of an opinion of someone else for stepping in, for saying the right thing. I actually was just telling a really great story about Virat and the troubles he had in Australia with driving the ball and nicking off. Eventually, in the fourth Test, I went to intervene and chat to him. And he was brilliant about it! And he actually wanted someone to chat to him," he said.However, Ten Doeschate admitted that initiating such a conversation with a player of Kohli's stature can be a delicate exercise. According to him, coaches need to consider not just what they want to communicate but also how and when they deliver the message."But my sense is, for a coach to go to a player like Virat Kohli and intervene and almost call them out on what's happening can be dangerous for you as a coach. And I think getting the wording right around that and how you deliver it is so important."The way the power shift has moved towards the players in the modern era does mean that a lot of coaches are scared to bring up topics or at least get talking about it."Ten Doeschate further explained that the objective of coaching should not necessarily be to convince a player to abandon his preferred approach. Instead, it should involve understanding the batter's thinking and finding ways to make adjustments without taking away what works for him.He recalled how Kohli explained his reasoning behind continuing to play the drive in the manner he did, making the exchange a discussion rather than a one-sided technical instruction."You don't have to agree. You might say, 'I want to drive on the up for these reasons,' and that's actually what happened with Virat. He really explained why he wanted to play in the way he played, and then you can tweak around that," Ten Doeschate revealed.The former assistant coach also highlighted the danger of introducing technical doubts into a batter's mind at the wrong moment. A player preparing to face a high-quality fast bowler could become distracted if he starts thinking too much about a particular aspect of his technique."There's always a risk that you sort of unsettle his frame of mind. You know, he might be in a really good place, and now you say, 'You know, I've noticed when you're pulling... you're just taking your eye off the ball.' Technically, you might want him to watch the ball a little bit longer, but now all of a sudden he's thinking about pulling, and he's got to go out and face Mitchell Starc. So that's not the time to do it," he said.Ten Doeschate revealed that the conversation with Kohli had been on his mind for some time before he eventually found an appropriate opportunity during a rain interruption.He said the repeated nature of Kohli's dismissals had prompted him to think carefully about how to raise the subject without making the batter feel that his technique was being questioned."In that situation, it had been bubbling away, and it was more a case of me building up the courage and delivering it in the right way. I was lucky enough to have a decent relationship with Virat. He's obviously not someone who needs a lot of coaching, and that was one thing that really stuck out-the manner of the dismissal being so same-same," he said.Explaining how he eventually approached the conversation, Ten Doeschate said he deliberately avoided making it sound like a direct criticism of Kohli's batting."So I had thought about it a lot, and I thought how I could deliver it. You know, I'm not going to go to him and say, 'Mate, you've got cover drives all over the show.' But I then worked out a time-it was during a rain break-where I could deliver it in quite a non-confrontational way. And credit to him, the way he took it on ended up being a really great discussion."While the intervention did not produce the desired outcome towards the end of the series, Ten Doeschate considered the experience an important lesson in communication and coaching."Unfortunately, it didn't deliver the results we wanted towards the back end of the series, but you know, I'd say if you can deliver it to someone like him, you can deliver it to anyone. Just finding the right way of dropping your message is really important," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia Sandpapergate: David Warner backs Usman Khawaja's claim entire team knew about 2018 ball-tampering plan in South Africa
articles.summary: David Warner said on Monday that former Australia team-mate Usman Khawaja's comments that the entire team had been ‌aware of the plan to tamper with the ball during a 2018 tour of South Africa were "100 per cent accurate"
articles.body:
Khawaja has claimed in recent days that players and coaching staff were aware of the ball-tampering that occurred in South Africa eight years ago , stating: "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us."

Warner also claimed the investigation held by Cricket Australia in the aftermath of the ball-tampering controversy was "rushed and botched".

Warner and fellow batters ‌Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were banned over the plan to rough up the ball with sandpaper ​during the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town.

In an excerpt of his autobiography released on Saturday, Khawaja said "open, lighthearted discussions" about tampering were ​not confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.

On ‌Sunday, he added that he had chosen to speak about the 'Sandpapergate' scandal now after promising childhood friend Warner that ​he would share his side of the story .

Until now, nobody else involved in the tour has ever admitted culpability.

The bowling unit of Pat Cummins - now Australia captain - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon even released a statement in 2021 denying they knew anything about the tactic.

Warner said in a video statement on Instagram: "People wanted to know it, you've come out and said it, and now people are saying, 'Why eight years on?' and talking about selling a book.

"This is Usman's story. This is what Usman believes. Uzzi wrote down every single thing from that day on. Uzzi, thank you.

"Now, this whole interview process was rushed and botched. Uzzi was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft. Uzzi was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me.

"We're not here to point fingers and we're not opening old wounds. It's about accountability, transparency and ensuring that the truth is properly examined."

Warner, who retired from cricket's traditional format in 2024 with 112 Test caps, said he decided to comment now after talking to his young daughters over recent days about what transpired in that match and later.

"Perhaps it's time people stop scrutinising the person asking for accountability and start asking those responsible for the investigation to provide it," he continued.

"Now, there have been a lot of statements and inaccuracies over the last eight years that were out in the media by people and there were a lot of people who stayed silent.

"The last couple of days I've been talking to my daughters and that's why it's taken me a couple of days to get this out, because I've had to tell them exactly what happened.

"Especially my 12-year-old Ivy, who wanted to know why we were holding her, why there were so many cameras and why we were crying on TV. That was a hard thing to do.

"But one thing I did say was, 'Girls, tell the truth, because lies will eventually come out'. It's a very tough time.

"This is for everyone in Australia. It's been the question that everyone's been asking. Uzzi, you said it how it is. It's 100 per cent accurate.

"It's been a tough time for my family, Steven and Cameron, no doubt, but this is what needed to come out. I fully support that, Uzzi."

Maddinson: Christmas comes along and people have books to sell

Australian opener Nic Maddinson said it was "disappointing" that Warner, Bancroft and Smith had to "relive" the situation.

"It's obviously disappointing that it keeps coming up," Maddinson told 10 Sport .

"But it's that time of year, isn't it? Christmas comes along and people have books to sell.

"Things come out. It's just disappointing.

"I think the three guys who were affected the most, it doesn't really help them at all to relive it. Especially over the past month having [had a] great series in South Africa.

"Obviously, the crowds weren't as hostile maybe as people expected. But that stuff is still there every day at airports, with the general public making comments here and there.

"So, I guess over time [it] would still wear them down. It's just popped up again. Start of the summer, going into a pretty big six months for the team, it is obviously probably pretty disappointing for those guys."

articles.title: Mushfiqur Rahim makes Bangladesh cricket history, becomes first to score 7,000 Test runs
articles.summary: Bangladesh veteran Mushfiqur Rahim added another landmark to his illustrious career, becoming the first batter from the country to score 7,000 runs in
articles.body: Bangladesh veteran Mushfiqur Rahim added another landmark to his illustrious career, becoming the first batter from the country to score 7,000 runs in Test cricket. The 39-year-old achieved the milestone in the ongoing second Test against West Indies in Sylhet, further cementing his place among Bangladesh's greatest players in the longest format.Mushfiqur reached the landmark when he took a single off West Indies spinner Roston Chase to move to nine runs in his innings. The veteran initially appeared unaware of the achievement, but acknowledged the moment after his teammates rose from their seats in the dressing room to applaud him.The milestone was another reward for Mushfiqur's remarkable longevity and consistency in Test cricket. He had missed the opening Test of the series because of a finger injury but returned for the second match to add another chapter to his career.From 5,000 to 7,000: Mushfiqur's remarkable journeyMushfiqur had already established himself as Bangladesh's leading Test run-scorer when he became the country's first batter to reach 5,000 runs in 2022 and 6,000 in 2024. He has now taken that record to another level, becoming the first Bangladesh player to breach the 7,000-run mark.He has accumulated 7,000 runs in his 107th Test, having needed only 25 innings to progress from 6,000 to 7,000. His tally includes 14 centuries, with his highest score being an unbeaten 219.Mominul Haque is second on Bangladesh's all-time Test run-scoring list with 5,293 runs, while former opener Tamim Iqbal is third. Mominul has scored 13 Test centuries, while Tamim has registered 10.Mushfiqur's latest achievement comes in a match in which his record for the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter in Tests was surpassed. Towhid Hridoy struck an unbeaten 242 earlier in the ongoing Sylhet Test, going past Mushfiqur's previous best of 219 not out.Bangladesh's most experienced Test cricketerHaving made his international debut in 2005, Mushfiqur is Bangladesh's most experienced Test cricketer. He became the first player from the country to feature in 100 Tests in November 2025 and is now appearing in his 107th match.His journey in the format has been one of steady evolution. Initially a lower-middle-order batter and wicketkeeper, Mushfiqur took 20 Tests to reach his first 1,000 runs. His batting responsibilities grew as he became a more established member of the side, particularly after taking over as Bangladesh captain in 2011.Over the years, he developed into one of the team's most dependable batters, producing crucial runs across conditions and against different opponents. His ability to maintain consistency over such a long career has been reflected in the latest milestone.Mushfiqur has also made significant contributions in limited-overs cricket, scoring 6,697 runs in ODIs and 1,495 in T20 Internationals. He has since retired from both formats, with Test cricket remaining the stage on which he continues to extend his legacy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'What justice is it to send KL Rahul at No.6?': Former India selector raises question amid New Zealand ODIs
articles.summary: KL Rahul’s batting position became a talking point after India’s second ODI against New Zealand in Wellington, with former India cricketer Krishnamachari
articles.body: KL Rahul’s batting position became a talking point after India’s second ODI against New Zealand in Wellington, with former India cricketer Krishnamachari Srikkanth questioning why Axar Patel was sent ahead of him.India were struggling at 39/3 when Axar walked in to bat. Although he had handled difficult situations on the same pitch before, he struggled against New Zealand’s bowling attack.The uneven bounce and short-pitched deliveries troubled him, and he eventually lost his wicket after scoring just seven runs off 17 balls.Rahul, who came in after Axar, looked much more comfortable on a pitch where most batters from both teams found it difficult to score. His performance raised questions about the decision to send him so low in the batting order.Srikkanth calls Rahul’s batting position unfairFormer India selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth strongly criticised the team management’s decision. Speaking on his YouTube channel, he said, “But what justice is it to send Rahul at No.6 after Axar Patel?”He also pointed out that Rahul is an experienced player who has scored international centuries at No.3 and No.4. “Gautam Gambhir needs to understand Rahul is a marquee player. He has scored centuries at No.3 and 4 for India. Yet, he is being reduced to such a role. It’s gross injustice,” said Srikkanth.He further praised Rahul’s ability to handle difficult conditions, saying, “He’s the only one who looked comfortable in the second ODI. Once the conditions are difficult, only two players step up – Virat Kohli and KL Rahul. If Rahul got out early in the last match, India were finished. How can you justify Axar batting ahead of him?”Gavaskar backs the decision to send Axar aheadHowever, former India captain Sunil Gavaskar had a different opinion. He supported the idea of sending a left-handed batter ahead of right-handers to disturb the opposition bowlers' rhythm.“The bowlers have slight difficulty if a left-handed batter comes because you have to change the line and length you would have for a right-hander. In trying to do that, your line can change slightly even to the right-hander, where more chances of getting runs are created,” Gavaskar explained.He added that such decisions do not always work, but that does not make them wrong.“There was nothing wrong with that thought process. If Axar had scored runs, you would have said how good the captaincy was. Such moves work at times and don’t work on other occasions, and it didn’t work this time. You also knew there was a solid player like Rahul after him. That’s why you experiment at times,” Gavaskar observed.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: England Test squad for South Africa: Uncapped spinner Liam Patterson-White called up and Jacob Bethell returns
articles.summary: England selectors name a 15-player squad for the three-Test series away to South Africa with uncapped spinner Liam Patterson-White earning a call-up; Shoaib Bashir dropped to Lions squad; Jacob Bethell returns to the Test squad following his knee injury during the summer
articles.body:
All-rounder Patterson-White helped Nottinghamshire win the Championship title in 2025 by taking 26 wickets and scoring 540 runs in 11 appearances, and then claimed 42 wickets and scored 474 runs in 14 appearances last season.

Jacob Bethell did not feature in August and September's 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to a knee problem that required surgery, but he is back to add to England's batting options for a tour that is live in full on Sky Sports across December and January in what will be Stephen Fleming's first series as head coach.

Jordan Cox deputised for Bethell at No 3 versus Pakistan, scoring a half-century in each of the three Tests at Headingley, Lord's and Edgbaston.

The Essex player's displays have opened up a selection dilemma, with possibly only three spots available between Cox, Bethell, Emilio Gay and Dan Lawrence.

Should England omit opener Gay, who has three fifties across his first six Tests since replacing Zak Crawley at the start of the summer, Cox or Bethell could potentially partner Ben Duckett at the top of the order.

Middle-order batter and part-time bowler Lawrence was recalled against Pakistan following Ben Stokes' international retirement and acted as the chief spinner as England deployed an all-pace frontline attack with great success.

England Men's national selector Marcus North said: "Liam Patterson-White's selection comes on the back of a strong summer in the Rothesay County Championship, when he took the most wickets of any spinner in Division One with 42 at an average of 25.11 and earned his first ECB development contract."

North: Carse can work way back into England team with Lions stint

Josh Tongue will be unavailable for the first Test in order to return to the UK for the birth of his first child with Brydon Carse , included in a strong England Lions squad, in position to replace him. Carse was dropped by England in the summer after an incident in Derby in August and was subsequently charged by the Cricket Regulator, with a verdict still to come.

Sam Curran is unavailable for the Test series as he is prioritising his wedding.

North confirmed "one or two players" from the Lions squad will be drafted into Fleming's playing group and did not rule out Carse.

"Obviously in the past few months under investigation, it's been a time where he [Carse] has stood back and it's been a time of reflection," North said, after the squad announcement.

"It's obviously been a challenging time for Brydon and it's one we probably haven't at times felt the demands of playing international cricket and what he was dealing with was necessarily right for Brydon or us.

"There has been several conversations between us, myself, (managing director) Rob Key and other people at the ECB with Brydon over this period and the conclusion is we feel he is in a place where we can introduce him back into an England environment.

"We feel the Lions is the right place for him to come.

"Come that first Test, with Josh Tongue unavailable, that will leave us with 14 players and this is where I feel we're using the Lions tour to our advantage.

"You can see there is a very strong bowling group that is in the Lions programme and that enables us to no doubt look at where they are at in competition and under training.

"They will be out there from the [November] 25th, the Lions players, with some of our red-ball Test players, Stephen Fleming will be out there at that time and that enables us to be as informed as possible to then bring one or two players across into that Test squad come that first Test."

England begin the South Africa series in Johannesburg on December 17, before the Boxing Day Test is held at Centurion and the series concludes in Cape Town from January 3.

They then meet the Proteas in three one-day internationals, with one game in Paarl (January 10) and two in Bloemfontein (January 13 and 15).

Bashir and Carse are joined in the Lions' red-ball squad by James Rew, who featured over the summer in England's Test team.

On Bashir's omission from the senior Test squad, North said: "He's someone that we do still have a very positive outlook for.

"We sit down looking at each Test series in isolation and we feel that Liam gives us the best balance and that spinner for this tour of South Africa. We will continue to be incredibly invested in Shoaib over the winter.

"He [Bashir] is still very young, but he's in a good place. He is determined and is continuing to grow and learn.

"We still value [him], and [he] will continue to develop and [we'll] see where we can get Shoaib in the coming months and year."

The six players in the Test squad, who are not involved in the upcoming white-ball series in Australia - Sam Cook, Gay, Lawrence, Patterson-White, Ollie Robinson and Jamie Smith - will fly out to South Africa early with the England Lions squad for a preparation camp in Pietermaritzburg on November 25.

Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Duckett and Joe Root will return to the UK immediately after the ODI series against Australia before flying to South Africa on December 2.

Harry Brook, Bethell and Cox will leave the tour of Australia after the fourth T20 in Sydney on November 29 and fly directly to South Africa.

England Men's Test tour of South Africa schedule

December 9-11: Warm-up match v CSA XI; Kingsmead Cricket Ground, Durban December 17-21: First Test; Wanderers Stadium, Johannesburg December 26-20: Second Test; Centurion Park, Centurion January 3-7: Third Test, Newlands Cricket Ground, Cape Town

England Lions tour of South Africa schedule

December 1: First 50-over match v South Africa A; Pietermaritzburg Oval, Pietermaritzburg December 4: Second 50-over match v South Africa A; Boland Park, Paarl December 6: Third 50-over match v South Africa A; Boland Park, Paarl December 10-13: First four-day match v South Africa A; Tuks Cricket Oval, Pretoria December 18-21: Second four-day match v South Africa A; Willowmoore Park, Benoni

articles.title: Brydon Carse given path to England return, Shoaib Bashir dropped and Liam Patterson-White called up
articles.summary: England open the door for Brydon Carse to return to Test cricket for the tour of South Africa by naming him in the Lions squad.
articles.body:
England have opened the door for Brydon Carse to return to Test cricket for the tour of South Africa by naming the pace bowler in the Lions squad.

Carse could come into the Test squad as cover for Josh Tongue, who will miss the opener to the three-Test series to be at the birth of his second child.

England have named a 15-man group for the series, which begins in Johannesburg on 17 December. Uncapped Nottinghamshire left-arm spinner Liam Patterson-White is called up for the first time, at the expense of Shoaib Bashir.

Carse has not been part of any England squad since being handcuffed - explained as arrested then de-arrested - outside a nightclub in Derby in August.

Although Derbyshire Police have ended their investigation into a potential assault, Carse has been charged by the Cricket Regulator, with a verdict still to come.

Carse has continued to play for Durham and has remained available for England selection since the Derby incident.

However, England have previously explained his absence by a need for Carse to spend time away from the international arena.

Speaking as the Test and Lions squads were announced on Monday, England selector Marcus North said: "The past few months, under investigation, there has been a time where he has stood back, a time of reflection.

"It's obviously been a challenging time for Brydon, it's one that we haven't felt that the demands of playing international cricket and what he was dealing with wasn't necessarily right for Brydon or for us.

"There have been numerous conversations over this period. The conclusion is we feel he is in a place where we feel we can introduce him back into the England environment and we feel the Lions is the right place for him to come."

England squad for three-Test series in South Africa: Joe Root (captain), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook, Sam Cook, Jordan Cox, Ben Duckett, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Liam Patterson-White, Ollie Robinson, Jamie Smith, Josh Tongue.

Tongue is missing England's one-day series in Australia with a toe injury and is due to see a specialist in the UK.

Depending on the status of his injury, he could play in England's only warm-up game ahead of the South Africa Tests before returning home for the birth, leaving the tourists a seamer light.

Carse will be competing with other Lions seamers Henry Crocombe, Olly Stone, Matthew Fisher, Eddie Jack, Matthew Potts and Mitchell Stanley for the chance to cover for Tongue.

And North confirmed England will call up "one or two" players to the senior squad.

"This is where I feel using the Lions tour to our advantage - we have a very strong bowling group in that Lions programme," he said.

"That enables us to have a look at where they are at, under competition and training."

The tour of South Africa will be England's first under new head coach Stephen Fleming.

With the white-ball team currently in Perth preparing for the first one-day against Australia on Friday, Fleming travelled from his home in New Zealand to meet with the rest of the management and select the Test squad.

Jacob Bethell returns to the Test team for the first time since July following a knee injury.

The left-hander's return creates congestion in the top order after Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox both featured in the 3-0 home win over Pakistan, with North confirming England are yet to settle on their top six for the first Test against South Africa.

All-rounder Sam Curran, touted as a potential replacement for former captain Ben Stokes, was not considered because he is getting married. The wedding was planned before Stokes announced his international retirement during the summer.

England Lions red-ball squad for two first-class matches in South Africa: Shoaib Bashir, Brydon Carse, James Coles, Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe, Matthew Fisher, Jack Haynes, George Hill, Eddie Jack, Ben Mayes, Ben McKinney, Ollie Pope, Matthew Potts, James Rew, Thomas Rew, Mitch Stanley, Olly Stone, Asa Tribe.

England Lions 50-over squad: Rehan Ahmed, Brydon Carse, Mason Crane, Adam Finch, Matthew Fisher, Calvin Harrison, Jack Haynes, George Hill, Ben Mayes, Ben McKinney, Ollie Pope, James Rew, Naavya Sharma, Ekansh Singh, Asa Tribe.

Bashir's omission is eye-catching, given the faith England showed in the off-spinner under Stokes and previous Test coach Brendon McCullum.

Given a debut at the age of 20 and after playing only six previous first-class matches, Bashir was fast-tracked as England's number-one spinner, becoming the youngest England bowler to 50 Test wickets in the process.

However, a broken hand and a lack of form meant he was not picked during last winter's 4-1 defeat in Australia, and conditions meant he bowled in only one of England's six home Tests during the past summer.

Bashir was still the only specialist red-ball spinner given a central contract last month, an indication he remained the first choice, though is now effectively dropped from a squad for the first time in his England career. The 23-year-old will instead join Carse in the Lions.

"Our investment hasn't changed," said North of Bashir. "He is still a very young man, he is someone who we still have a very positive outlook for.

"We look at each Test series in isolation, and we feel Liam gives us the best balance and that spinner for this tour. We continue to be incredibly invested in Shoaib over the winter."

Patterson-White, who turned 28 on Sunday, is called up on the back of strong form for Nottinghamshire and after being given an England development contract.

Last season, his 42 wickets were the most by a spinner in Division One of the County Championship, while he can contribute with the bat too, having made three first-class hundreds.

Patterson-White may also have benefitted from new coach Fleming's links to Nottinghamshire, the county he once captained.

"Liam has got some great attributes," said North. "There is a lot of consistency with Liam and his bowling.

"We feel that has really come and matured during the past two seasons at Nottinghamshire. He has the ability to hold an end, but also get into the game at the back end.

"We're really excited to see Liam in that Test environment. It's recognition of his development over the past year or so."

The Test squad will arrive in South Africa in different groups, with some joining the Lions in late November and others after returning to the UK following their part in the three one-dayers in Australia.

From the Test players who are also involved in the T20 series in Australia, white-ball captain Harry Brook, Bethell and Cox will miss the fifth and final match of the series in order to travel to South Africa.

For Brook, it will be the first England game he has missed since the T20 tour of Ireland last September. In his absence, all-rounder Will Jacks will captain England for the first time.

articles.body: MUMBAI: In a major turnaround in fortunes for SKY, the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) on Monday appointed India's 2026 T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav as Mumbai skipper for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy.TOI had exclusively reported in its November 5 edition that the veteran batter was set to be the white-ball captain this season."The MCA is pleased to announce the Mumbai Senior Men's squad for the upcoming Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, India's premier domestic T20 competition. India T20 captain Suryakumar Yadav will lead the Mumbai side, bringing his vast international experience, leadership and explosive batting prowess to the team. The squad features a blend of experienced international and domestic players along with promising young talent, reflecting Mumbai's continued commitment to excellence and nurturing the next generation of cricketers," the MCA said in a statement.Speaking about his appointment as captain, Suryakumar said: "It is always a matter of immense pride to represent Mumbai. I am honoured to lead this talented group in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Mumbai has a rich cricketing legacy and a winning culture, and we will look to uphold those traditions. We have a good mix of experienced players and exciting young talent, and I am confident that the team will come together, play with intensity and give its best in every match. Our aim is to go all the way and bring the trophy home."On Monday morning, SKY captained a team against a side led by Sarfaraz Khan as Mumbai played an intra-squad practice match at the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India.On October 6, the 36-year-old batter was overlooked by the Mumbai selectors despite making himself available for the entire Ranji Trophy season. articles.title: Brydon Carse: England pave way for fast bowler's Test return ahead of South Africa series and will continue to 'invest' in Shoaib Bashir
articles.summary: Brydon Carse was included in England Lions' 15-man squad for their upcoming tour of South Africa and could be in line for a Test return; spinner Shoaib Bashir drops out of senior red ball squad; watch England's three-Test series vs South Africa live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 31-year-old was dropped from the Test squad midway through their summer series against Pakistan after he was arrested and later 'de-arrested' following an incident outside a Derby nightclub in August .

Derbyshire police ended their investigation into the incident in September, but Carse was later charged by the Cricket Regulator and is yet to learn his fate.

Carse has since spent some time away from the international scene, returning to play for Durham in the County Championship.

"It's obviously been a challenging time for Brydon," England national selector Marcus North said after naming both the senior and Lions squads to tour South Africa from early December.

"There's been numerous conversations between myself Rob Key (managing director of men's cricket), and other people at the ECB with Brydon over this period.

"The conclusion is we feel he's in a place where we can introduce him back into the England environment.

"We feel the Lions is the right place for him."

North also fielded questions on whether Carse could return to the squad as cover for Josh Tongue for the side's three-Test series against South Africa, live on Sky Sports .

Tongue has been ruled out of England's white-ball tour of Australia due to a toe injury and he will also miss the first Test in Johannesburg on December 17 to return home for the birth of his second child.

"Come that first Test, Josh Tongue is unavailable," North said. "So that will leave us with 14 players.

"This is where I feel we're using the Lions to our advantage, you can see there that we've got a very strong bowling group in that programme."

He added: "Stephen Fleming will be out there at that time. So it enables us to be as informed as possible to if we need to bring one or two players across into the squad come that first Test."

'Not the end of the road for Bashir just yet'

Sky Sports News' James Cole analyses the key talking points:

"Marcus North insists Shoaib Bashir still has a big international future, but dropping him for the upcoming tour of South Africa marks a definite change of direction.

"Bashir was fast-tracked into the Test side by Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum having played only six first-class games.

"He was heavily backed by the previous regime, but with Joe Root and Stephen Fleming now in charge of the Test team, his future looks less certain.

"Bashir is 23 and remains the only specialist red-ball spinner with an ECB central contract, so it's not the end of the road by any stretch - but it does feel like a significant speed bump."

Patterson-White call-up shows ECB will reward county players

"Liam Patterson-White has been rewarded for his excellent form for Nottinghamshire. His 42 County Championship wickets last season was the most by a Division One spinner.

"What's more - and in stark contrast to Bashir - he's also a very capable batter who has three first-class hundreds to his name.

"His selection is also another sign the ECB are committed to rewarding form in the County Championship, something that was highlighted for improvement in the post-Ashes review."

"Jacob Bethell will return from injury for the South Africa tour, but where he will bat remains unclear. In Bethell's absence, Jordan Cox averaged 50 batting at three during the summer's Pakistan series.

"North said England haven't yet decided their top six for South Africa and didn't rule out Bethell opening the batting. It's a good problem to have but one of Fleming and Root's most pressing issues is to figure out how to accommodate all their best batters."

articles.title: 'It's ridiculous': Ex-India coach questions Yashasvi Jaiswal's ODI snub
articles.summary: Former India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate has questioned India's decision to keep Yashasvi Jaiswal out of the ODI team.
articles.body: Former India assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate has questioned India's decision to keep Yashasvi Jaiswal out of the ODI team. He feels it is difficult to understand why a batter with so much talent and hunger to score runs is not getting a regular place in the side.In six ODI matches, the left-hander has scored 285 runs, including two centuries, at an average of 71.25. However, despite these numbers, he has not been able to secure a regular place in India's white-ball teams.With the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching, Jaiswal's chances of becoming a regular member of the first-choice team remain uncertain.Speaking on the TalkSport Cricket Podcast, ten Doeschate spoke about Jaiswal's hunger to score runs and his disappointment when he misses out on big scores."He is so hungry to do well. You know, even when he gets runs but doesn't get a big one, the genuine disappointment in leaving runs out there, you can see it really hurts him. He is also, just touching on the ODI point, he is desperate to play ODI cricket as well. He doesn't get into the team, which is - it's crazy," said Doeschate.‘It's ridiculous’: Ten Doeschate on Jaiswal's ODI omissionThe former India assistant coach went a step further and described Jaiswal's absence from the ODI team as ridiculous. He also spoke about the young batter's hard work and dedication."It's ridiculous. There are some players we were chatting about yesterday who aren't in the team. But also just to be clear, you know, I wasn't the batting coach, so I didn't have that direct access to players in terms of working that closely with them. It was so I'd chip in here and there and maybe complement what the batting coach and the head coach were saying. But yeah, certainly very, very hungry, works very, very hard. One of those strange situations where he's actually not a great netter," he added.Jaiswal's fearless approach against StarcTen Doeschate also recalled Jaiswal's performance during India's Test tour of Australia in 2024. He remembered how the youngster took on Mitchell Starc's pace and bounce in the first Test in Perth, despite struggling to deal with short balls during the practice sessions."I'll never forget, it happened in Australia, that whole build-up in Perth. And within the first three overs of the first Test match, Starc had bowled a 150k bouncer and he just pulled him in front of square. He just didn't look like he could play the short ball in the nets," he said.Jaiswal in good form ahead of New Zealand Test seriesMeanwhile, Jaiswal has been among the runs in the unofficial Test series against New Zealand A. The three-match series ended in a 0-0 draw after the fourth day's play in the third match was abandoned.Jaiswal scored 17 and 5 in the first unofficial Test. He had a difficult start in the second match, getting out for a duck in the first innings. However, he bounced back with an unbeaten 155 in the second innings.The left-hander continued his good form in the third unofficial Test, scoring another century with 102 runs.Devdutt Padikkal, Jaiswal, Dhruv Jurel, Sai Sudharsan and Washington Sundar also got valuable time in the middle during the series. The first three batters scored four centuries between them.The focus will now shift to the two-Test series between India and New Zealand. articles.body: Buoyed by their pacers’ impressive performances in the first two games but concerned about their senior batters’ struggles in seamer-friendly conditions, India will once again bank on Virat Kohli’s brilliance and KL Rahul’s composure as they look to seal the series against an injury hit New Zealand in the third ODI in Hamilton on Tuesday.India lead the five-match series 2-0, but barring Kohli’s majestic 74 at Eden Park and Rahul’s finishing touch in Wellington, the rest of the batting lineup has struggled. Skipper Shubman Gill, former captain Rohit Sharma and vice-captain Shreyas Iyer have all found it difficult to cope with the pace and bounce on offer, although Iyer chipped in with a useful 30 in the second ODI.Having been dismissed for 0 and 37 in the first two games, Gill will be keen to get a substantial score while helping India wrap up the series. He will miss the final two ODIs and turn his attention to redball preparations ahead of the first Test in Wellington on Nov 19. A good knock would provide a timely confidence boost, especially as he will not have a red-ball warm-up game. Iyer will lead India in the final two ODIs in Tauranga.India will also hope their two senior Mumbai batters, Rohit (0 and 23) and Iyer (15 and 30), come up with substantial contributions. Both showed glimpses of form during the tricky chase in Wellington, but will want to make a bigger impact.As has been the trend in the series, the third ODI at Seddon Park could also be affected by rain. Cold and damp conditions are likely to offer seam movement and extra bounce, making life difficult for batters once again.‘Rahul has played some unbelievable innings’India head coach Gautam Gambhir may also need to reconsider his decision to promote Axar Patel to No. 5 ahead of Rahul, who has looked more assured in the middle order and equally comfortable finishing games at No. 6.The move to send Axar ahead of Rahul is intended to introduce a left-hander into a top order dominated by right-handers. However, Axar has struggled against pace and steep bounce. In Wellington, Rahul remained unbeaten on 26, holding the innings together. He handled the short ball confidently and kept India ahead of the DLS par score before rain ended the contest in 26 overs, with the visitors securing a four-run win.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak praised Rahul’s versatility and ability to adapt to different roles.“I think KL Rahul’s biggest advantage is that he can open in red-ball cricket and bat in the middle order in white-ball cricket. Whenever required, he can also go with five overs left. His record there is also very good. So, he plays according to the team’s needs,” Kotak said on Monday. “He has played some unbelievable innings, and he never looks under pressure,” he said.India’s biggest positive has been the form of their fast bowlers. Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi have all impressed. With the Test series approaching, India would also like to give experienced pacer Mohammed Siraj some game time.New Zealand, meanwhile, have struggled to find their rhythm. Mitchell Santner has lost the toss in both matches, allowing India to exploit the damp conditions. The absence of openers Devon Conway, who is recovering from concussion, and injured Rachin Ravindra has further weakened their batting.The hosts will also be without pacer Blair Tickner, who suffered a concussion. Kristian Clarke has been called up as his replacement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pacers Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi to stay back to help Test squad: Sitanshu Kotak
articles.summary: Even as India contest the ODI series against New Zealand, the team management is preparing to switch into Test mode.
articles.body: Even as India contest the ODI series against New Zealand, the team management is preparing to switch into Test mode. Pacers Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi will stay back to help the squad prepare for the two-Test series beginning Nov 19, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said on Saturday.Kotak said the support staff could be split after the third ODI, with head coach Gautam Gambhir remaining with the white-ball squad and Kotak and bowling coach Morne Morkel travelling to Wellington to oversee Test preparations.“Gautam will have to stay here with the ODI squad, as the World Cup is coming up, and Sairaj Bahutule will probably stay back too. Morne, some other staff members and I will travel to Wellington. This is the current plan, though Gautam will take the final call. We want to ensure the Test players get adequate preparation, with their workload, fitness and practice taken care of, as much as conditions allow. Arshdeep, Nabi and Gurnoor will, if I am not mistaken, stay back for the Tests,” Kotak said.Players with the India ‘A’ team in Christchurch will join the Test squad in Wellington. Kotak said the lively ODI pitches had offered useful preparation. “The wicket in both ODIs had swing and when it stopped after four to six overs, there was seam movement and a little awkward bounce. In the Test match, the same thing can happen, only the ball will be red. With thicker grass and these conditions, you can get an idea in one day also. It is challenging,” he said.Kotak also pointed to the three India ‘A’ matches as an important part of the build-up for batters and bowlers, saying they would help players understand lengths and release points. India’s Test players are scheduled to begin a preparatory camp on Nov 11, giving them five to six sessions before the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Our batters have been challenged': New Zealand coach Luke Ronchi praises India's pacers
articles.summary: India’s young pace quartet of Arshdeep Singh, Auqib Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Gurnoor Brar has played a decisive role in the visitors taking a 2-0 lead in
articles.body: India’s young pace quartet of Arshdeep Singh, Auqib Nabi, Anshul Kamboj and Gurnoor Brar has played a decisive role in the visitors taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match ODI series against New Zealand. The four have claimed 17 of the 20 New Zealand wickets to fall across the first two ODIs.New Zealand batting coach Luke Ronchi admitted India’s seamers had posed tough questions for his side.“They’ve been really good. They’re asking questions of batters and it’ll be quite cool for them,” Ronchi said at the pre-match news conference in Hamilton on Monday. “They’re going into games where the ball isn’t flying around, the ball is actually assisting them and they’ll be happy with that.”Ronchi said the most impressive aspect was the way India’s young attack had adjusted from bowling on flatter subcontinental surfaces to finding the right lengths in more helpful conditions. “They are so used to bowling on flat wickets, it’s realising what is the right length, the right line. The ball is swinging a bit and it’s about knowing how to bowl the way they want to bowl to make it hard for the batters,” he said.“They’ve done that really well. They’ve challenged our batters, taken wickets early and made different impacts in different games. It’s exciting to see younger guys come into the game, perform and push their case to be playing more and more.”Ronchi said the seam-friendly surfaces in the ODI series would help both teams prepare for the two-Test series starting on Nov 19.“Technically, yeah, they will, because that’s traditionally what we have here for Test cricket — greener surfaces,” he said. “That Wellington surface was more of a Test-type surface, so it’s grasping hold of that and realising that. It will help both teams.“At the moment, the bowlers have got the upper hand, so there’s nothing wrong with that. Around the world, especially in India, if teams don’t make 400, you’re in trouble, so it’s just ridiculous. The bowlers have an opportunity to get some conditions, but you still have to bowl well on them. Both teams have been doing that.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'You always have the gun to your head': Ravi Shastri on life as Team India head coach
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri feels coaching is tougher than playing cricket or working as a commentator.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri feels coaching is tougher than playing cricket or working as a commentator. He said the job comes with huge responsibility and pressure, as a coach has little control over what happens once the players step onto the field.Known for his straight-talking nature and energetic commentary, Shastri shared his views on the three roles in an interview with Sky Sport's Ian Smith.When asked which one he found the toughest, the former India coach picked coaching."Yeah, the toughest would be coaching, right. See, no, because you are nothing in your control once the players leave and get onto the field. You have the bat, ball when you're playing, the mic when you're broadcasting. But once the players go out, you know, you can only twiddle your thumbs. And it comes with immense responsibility. You know, the expectations of the country are such. COVID, no COVID, you got to win, you know, game after game. So there's no hiding behind that," Shastri said.He also spoke about the pressure that comes with the job and the satisfaction of delivering results."You know, you always have the gun to your head. But if you pull it off and you're successful, I mean, then the rewards, it's very rewarding. Gives you tons of respect. And, you know, makes you enjoy what you're doing and gives you that kind of job satisfaction with nothing else gave you," he said.Shastri was India's head coach from July 2017 to November 2021. His tenure saw the team achieve several major milestones, including two historic Test series victories in Australia.India won their first-ever Test series in Australia during the 2018-19 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. They followed it up with another memorable 2-1 series win in 2020-21, despite several injury setbacks.Under Shastri, India also held the No. 1 position in the ICC Test rankings for 42 months and reached the final of the inaugural World Test Championship in 2021. The team also made it to the semi-finals of the 2019 ODI World Cup.‘The only way we can hang in here is if we are passionate’Shastri also looked back at his journey in broadcasting and spoke about what has kept him connected to cricket for so many years.He said his passion for the game has been the biggest reason behind his long association with the sport, despite having opportunities to explore other fields."[On his journey into broadcasting] it's amazing how life can take you in various places. And particularly the cricketing life. I mean it's captured us. I mean obviously you love the game. I mean you know to stay involved because you would have had many, many opportunities to break away and do other things with your stature in India. But you stayed with the game. And I love it. I mean the only way we can hang in here if we are passionate about the game," Shastri said."If you're not passionate about the game, you don't love the game, you won't be here this long with showing that kind of enthusiasm for every game day after day. You know, whether it's with you, the way you commentated on that World Cup final, you know, a close finish, you were calling it at the end. Fabulous. And we've called many finals in the end, you know, right through our careers. And it's a privilege, you know, when someone understands the game, understands the discipline of television, you know, and then to work that for that length of time. It's fun," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Next Delhi Capitals captain after Axar Patel exit: R Ashwin sends warning to DC regarding Rishabh Pant
articles.summary: R Ashwin issued a blunt warning to DC against burdening Rishabh Pant with captaincy amid CSK trade links.
articles.body:
Delhi Capitals are reportedly in talks with Chennai Super Kings over a player trade.

A cryptic social media photograph from Chennai has set the cricketing rumour mill spinning.

Ravichandran Ashwin has shared a clear view on Delhi's trade targets and captaincy choices.

Why did R Ashwin warn Delhi Capitals about Rishabh Pant amid Axar Patel trade rumours?

Delhi Capitals may soon be hunting for a new captain, and Ravichandran Ashwin has already cautioned the franchise to be careful about how it handles Rishabh Pant. His warning comes amid reports that DC have opened trade discussions with Chennai Super Kings, and that their current skipper, Axar Patel, could be the player who changes hands.

The left-arm spinning all-rounder is reportedly at the centre of the talks, which could take him to the five-time IPL champions. It is not yet clear, however, which player Delhi would ask for in return, so the deal remains very much a matter of speculation for now.

Chennai themselves did little to cool things down. The franchise shared a photograph on its official X account that shows its own captain, Ruturaj Gaikwad, deep in a relaxed chat with Patel. The picture was taken in New Zealand once India had wrapped up a win in the second ODI on Saturday.

Supporters were quick to treat the post as a hint, and talk of a possible IPL trade between the two sides gained momentum.

Delhi brought Pant back to the franchise from Lucknow Super Giants straight after the IPL 2026 season ended, which means the experienced wicketkeeper-batter is home again after two years away.

KL Rahul is also part of the squad, so DC now have two senior names who could lead the side on the field. That depth gives the management some freedom, and it is easy to see why they might feel tempted to let Patel go.

Ashwin accepts that the deal could happen, but he believes Delhi must be wary of several things if they let their captain walk out. In his view, the franchise should ask for a player such as Dewald Brevis or Noor Ahmed in return. Kuldeep Yadav has already moved to Lucknow in the deal that brought Pant back, so Delhi are short of spin options at the moment.

On his YouTube channel 'Ash ki Baat', the former India spinner started by questioning the very logic of the trade. He also pointed out what Axar's arrival would mean for the Chennai squad, as it would leave one of their overseas spinners without a role.

"Why is this trade even possible? Think about why this trade could even make sense. A player of this commodity can give them balance. If Axar comes, they will not need Akeal Hosein at all. Why is Delhi even thinking, if at all they are?" he said.

Ashwin then moved on to the players he would want Delhi to chase, and he leaned on Brevis's recent record with a Sourav Ganguly-coached side as the main argument.

"Where Ganguly was the mentor at Pretoria Capitals, Brevis did well single-handedly, and he will rate him. They might go after him. And Brevis is with CSK. They let Kuldeep go, so Noor Ahmed could be enticing too," he added.

Who will captain Delhi Capitals if Axar Patel leaves? Ashwin prefers KL Rahul over Rishabh Pant

An Axar exit would leave Delhi with the big job of finding a new leader, and Pant is the name that comes to mind first because he has captained the franchise before.

Ashwin, however, does not want the left-hander to be handed the role again. He thinks veteran opener KL Rahul is a far better fit to fill the gap if the trade goes through, and instead Pant should be left free to express himself as a player, without the weight of leadership on his shoulders.

"It might be possible. It can happen. KL Rahul is a good and experienced option. Pant needs to play freely. If someone can convince him not to take captaincy and play freely as a player, it is Dada (Ganguly). No one else can. It may not be a bad call," Ashwin said.

Why Delhi Capitals should resist the urge to trade Axar Patel to Chennai Super Kings

From a purely cricketing point of view, Delhi should hold on to Axar Patel rather than hand him over to Chennai. Indian all-rounders who can bowl four tight overs of left-arm spin and then bat anywhere between No. 5 and No. 7 are among the rarest assets in the IPL, and that makes Axar close to irreplaceable in the way DC build their side.

The destination makes the idea even harder to defend. Chepauk has long suited spinners, so Axar would solve what is arguably Chennai's biggest tactical gap, and Delhi would be strengthening a direct rival in the process. It is difficult to see the benefit in that, however attractive the cash or the swap might look on paper.

Unless Chennai offer something extraordinary, such as a proven Indian middle-order powerhouse or a marquee fast bowler, the numbers simply do not add up for Delhi. Losing their captain and their most dependable utility player would also leave them hunting for both a leader and a spinner at the same time, and that is a lot to ask of any franchise in one window.

The presence of Pant and Rahul gives the management comfort on the leadership front, but comfort is not a reason to sell. Ashwin's own list of targets shows how thin the market is for a like-for-like replacement. DC would be wise to keep Axar and let the trade talk fade away.

articles.title: Why Shubman Gill is captaining India for the last time in New Zealand ODI series
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill is leading India for the final time in the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill is leading India for the final time in the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand. The third ODI at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday is his last match as both captain and player in the five-match series.Gill will miss the fourth and fifth ODIs as the BCCI has decided to rest some key players ahead of the two-Test series against New Zealand.After a two-hour delay due to rain and a wet outfield, India won the toss and elected to bowl in the third ODI. The visitors, who lead the series 2-0, are looking to complete a clean sweep.The first two matches were also affected by rain. India won the opening ODI in Auckland by five wickets while chasing a revised DLS target of 143 in 22.2 overs.In the second ODI in Wellington, India were declared winners under the DLS method after rain stopped play with the visitors at 113/7 while chasing 135. India were four runs ahead of the DLS par score at that stage.Why is Shubman Gill playing his last match of the ODI series?The BCCI had announced separate squads for the first three and the last two ODIs against New Zealand. The decision was taken to manage the workload of key players ahead of the Test series.Gill was named captain for the first three ODIs, while Shreyas Iyer will take charge of the team in the final two matches.The BCCI also named Iyer as vice-captain for the first three matches and Ishan Kishan as vice-captain for the last two ODIs.Gill, along with KL Rahul and some other key players, will not be part of the squad for the remaining two matches. They will get time to prepare for the upcoming Test series.Tight schedule ahead of India-New Zealand TestsThe fourth and fifth ODIs will be played on November 13 and 15 respectively at Mount Maunganui.The first Test of the two-match series will begin on November 19 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.This leaves the Indian players with just four days between the final ODI and the start of the Test series. The short gap makes workload management important, especially for players expected to feature in both formats.The two-Test series is also important for India's chances of reaching the World Test Championship final. The team management will want its key players to be fresh and ready for the longer format.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Anshul Kamboj explains why New Zealand feels like Haryana: 'Similar weather and wickets'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Anshul Kamboj may be experiencing New Zealand conditions for the first time, but the Indian pacer is hardly finding them unfamiliar.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anshul Kamboj may be experiencing New Zealand conditions for the first time, but the Indian pacer is hardly finding them unfamiliar. The cold weather and seamer-friendly pitches have reminded him of winter in Haryana, where he has been honing his bowling skills since the age of 13. That familiarity appears to be working in his favour, with Kamboj making an impressive start to his maiden ODI assignment in New Zealand.Coming into the playing XI as a change, Kamboj has troubled the New Zealand batters with his accuracy, disciplined line and hard lengths. He returned figures of 2/22 in the first ODI at Eden Park and followed it up with 2/25 in the second match, making an immediate impression with the ball."I started playing when I was 13 years old. I play for Haryana. So it's like similar kind of, what can I say, weather and wickets as well in Haryana," Kamboj told the host broadcasters.Having grown up bowling in conditions similar to those in New Zealand, the 25-year-old has looked comfortable on the bouncy tracks at Auckland's Eden Park and Wellington's Basin Reserve.Accuracy remains Kamboj's biggest weaponWhile the conditions have suited his style, Kamboj is not looking to rely solely on the assistance available from the pitches. The Haryana pacer believes accuracy and adapting to the demands of the surface and match situation remain crucial to his success."It's about accuracy and the perfect line and length, according to the wicket and the situation. It's working for me right now, so I'm just focusing on that," he said.His preparation also included an India A outing, which helped him understand the conditions and identify the right lengths to bowl in New Zealand."Actually, it was just about acclimatising to the weather. The wicket was a bit nippy, and I just wanted to understand the right lengths and the right areas where I need to bowl. I'm just focusing on that," Kamboj explained.The early returns suggest that the preparation has paid off, with his disciplined approach making him an effective option in India's pace attack.CSK stint adds to learning curveKamboj's impressive international start comes on the back of a breakthrough 2026 IPL season with Chennai Super Kings, where he picked up 21 wickets in 14 matches.The opportunity to be around Mahendra Singh Dhoni and former head coach Stephen Fleming during his CSK stint also contributed to his development. Kamboj described the experience as an important learning phase, stressing that he continues to focus on improving rather than getting carried away by results."Actually, that was a good learning experience for me, and I'm still learning a lot. I'm just making sure that I'm learning in the right way, not thinking too much about the results, but focusing on what I need to do and what I need to do on the field as well," he said.For Kamboj, representing India has been another special milestone, particularly after years of working his way through domestic cricket."Actually, I'm excited and very happy as well, as I'm playing for my national team. It's everyone's dream to play for their national team, so it's pretty much exciting," he said.With two impressive performances already behind him, Kamboj will look to carry his accuracy and confidence into the remainder of the New Zealand tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Salman Butt found himself in an embarrassing situation during a live television broadcast ahead of the first Test
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Salman Butt found himself in an embarrassing situation during a live television broadcast ahead of the first Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka.Butt was giving a pitch report before the start of the match when he suddenly lost his train of thought. He struggled to continue his analysis and repeatedly apologised while standing in front of the camera.‘Salman bhai live hai’: Camera crew comes to the rescueThe moment became even more awkward when Butt started saying "Sorry, sorry, sorry, sorry, sorry..." on live television.The camera crew could be heard trying to alert him in the background."Salman bhai live hai, Salman bhai live hai!" (Salman brother, we are live!), they told the former Pakistan captain.The incident quickly caught attention on social media, with the video of Butt's on-air mistake going viral.Salman Butt's international careerButt represented Pakistan in all three formats of international cricket. He played 33 Tests, 78 ODIs and 24 T20Is during his career.In Test cricket, he scored 1,889 runs, including three centuries and 10 half-centuries. In ODIs, he made 2,725 runs, with eight centuries and 14 half-centuries. He also scored 595 runs in T20Is.Pakistan vs Sri Lanka: Playing XIsMeanwhile, Sri Lanka won the toss and elected to field in the first Test against Pakistan.Pakistan (Playing XI): Azan Awais, Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, Babar Azam (c), Saud Shakeel, Salman Agha, Ghazi Ghori (wk), Arafat Minhas, Razaullah, Mohammad Abbas, Saqib Khan.Sri Lanka (Playing XI): Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Lahiru Udara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva, Kusal Mendis (wk/c), Sonal Dinusha, Milan Priyanath Rathnayake, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We weren’t aware’: Mitchell Starc stands by his version of Sandpapergate despite David Warner backing Usman Khawaja
articles.summary: Australian fast bowler Mitchell Starc has stood by his version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, insisting that his recollection of the infamous
articles.body: Australian fast bowler Mitchell Starc has stood by his version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, insisting that his recollection of the infamous Sandpapergate episode has not changed, even as former teammate David Warner publicly backed Usman Khawaja's explosive claims about the controversy.Starc's response comes a day after Warner threw his weight behind Khawaja, describing the former Australia opener's revelations as “100% accurate” and questioning the credibility of Cricket Australia's investigation into the incident.Khawaja, in his autobiography Sabr, has claimed that the knowledge of the ball-tampering operation extended beyond the three players who were punished — Steve Smith, Warner and Cameron Bancroft — and that the entire Australian dressing room, including players and support staff, should have accepted collective responsibility.Starc, however, maintained that his position remained consistent with the statement issued by Australia's bowling quartet in 2021, which denied prior knowledge of a foreign object being used to alter the ball.Starc stands by 2021 statement after Warner backs KhawajaSpeaking at an event marking the launch of Australia's summer of cricket, Starc said he had not followed the renewed debate closely but made it clear that his recollection of the events remained unchanged.“I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair,” Starc said, as quoted by Fox Sports.“Obviously there are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process at the time and since. I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers, but, from where I stand, my opinion hasn't changed, and my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021,” he added.Starc also reiterated that the bowlers were unaware of any foreign substance being taken onto the field to tamper with the ball during the Cape Town Test.“We weren't aware anything was taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town,” he said.In 2021, Starc, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon had issued a joint statement after their integrity was questioned over the scandal. The quartet said they did not know a foreign substance had been taken onto the field until they saw the footage on the stadium's big screen at Newlands.Starc also addressed Khawaja's claim that sandpaper had been used during the preceding Test in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha. He said he had no prior knowledge of the alleged incident and left it to those making the claims to explain further.Warner calls Khawaja's revelations '100% accurate'Warner, one of the three players handed a 12-month ban by Cricket Australia after the Cape Town incident, publicly backed Khawaja in a video posted on Instagram.“It's been eight years since I've spoken on this topic. And Uzzie (Usman Khawaja), I throw my full support behind you. I thank you for what you've done. It's 100% accurate what you've said. Now everyone knows the truth. It's out there. People wanted to know it; you've come out and said it, and now people are saying, 'Why eight years on?' Talking about selling a book—this is Usman's story. This is what Usman believes,” Warner said.Warner also questioned why Khawaja, who was sitting next to Bancroft during the Cape Town Test, was not interviewed as part of Cricket Australia's investigation.“Now, this whole interview process was rushed and botched. Uzzie was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft; Uzzie was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me,” he said.“It's about accountability, transparency, ensuring that the truth is properly examined. And perhaps it's time people stop scrutinising the person asking for accountability and start asking those responsible for the investigation to provide it,” Warner added.He also revealed that the renewed discussion had forced him to explain the events and their aftermath to his daughters, particularly his 12-year-old Ivy, who wanted to know why the family had been surrounded by cameras and why they were crying on television.“That was a hard thing to do. But one thing I did say is, 'Girls, tell the truth, because lies will eventually get out,'” Warner said.He concluded by reiterating his support for Khawaja, saying: “It's been a tough time for my family, Steve and Cameron no doubt, but this is what needed to come out. I fully support that, Uzzie.”Cricket Australia rules out fresh investigationThe renewed claims have also brought Cricket Australia's original findings back into focus. The board's 2018 investigation concluded that Smith, Warner and Bancroft were involved in the ball-tampering plot, while the other members of the squad were cleared of wrongdoing.Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg said the governing body would not reopen the investigation despite the fresh revelations in Khawaja's book.“There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others,” Greenberg said.“We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman, and our position hasn't changed on that.”Greenberg added that Cricket Australia did not see a compelling reason to revisit the matter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
