articles.title: India vs New Zealand: No play in Hamilton! Rain washes out third ODI, India remain 2-0 up
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rain played spoilsport once again as the third ODI between India and New Zealand was called off at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rain played spoilsport once again as the third ODI between India and New Zealand was called off at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday. Despite a delay of more than two hours, the weather did not allow any play. The umpires eventually decided to abandon the match after rain returned and made conditions unsuitable for cricket.India continue to lead the five-match series 2-0.The two teams will now travel to Mount Maunganui for the final two ODIs, scheduled to be played on November 13 and 15.Rain washes out third ODI after tossIndia captain Shubman Gill won the toss for the third consecutive time in the ODI series and elected to bowl. The toss was originally scheduled for 2:30 PM local time (7:00 AM IST) but was delayed by more than two hours due to rain and a wet outfield. The match was later reduced to 40 overs per side.However, just as the ground staff were removing the covers to prepare for the match, rain returned and forced them to cover the pitch again.There was still enough time to play a 20-over match, but the weather showed no signs of improving. With the local cut-off time of 7:50 PM (12:20 PM) approaching, the umpires decided to call off the match.The forecast had already predicted a 90 per cent chance of rain throughout the day.India take unassailable 2-0 leadIndia had won the first two matches of the series, both of which were affected by rain. The visitors won the opening ODI in Auckland by five wickets while chasing a revised target under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method.In the second ODI in Wellington, India registered a four-run victory under the DLS method to take a 2-0 lead.With the third match ending without a result, India cannot lose the series. New Zealand will now have to win the remaining two matches to draw the series.The washout also ended New Zealand's run of 11 consecutive bilateral ODI series victories at home. South Africa hold the record with 17 successive home ODI series wins between 2002 and 2007.Shubman Gill's last ODI, Shreyas Iyer to lead IndiaThe third ODI was also the final match of the series for Shubman Gill and senior wicketkeeper-batter KL Rahul. Both players will now join India's Test squad in Wellington. Kuldeep Yadav, Anshul Kamboj and Mohammed Siraj will also link up with the Test team.Shreyas Iyer will take charge of India for the remaining two ODIs in Gill's absence.The fourth and fifth ODIs will be played at Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15 respectively.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Scotland suspended cricket ties with Afghanistan outside ICC events
articles.summary: Cricket Scotland has decided to suspend cricketing engagement with Afghanistan outside International Cricket Council (ICC) events, citing the Taliban
articles.body: Cricket Scotland has decided to suspend cricketing engagement with Afghanistan outside International Cricket Council (ICC) events, citing the Taliban government's treatment of women and girls and wider human rights concerns.The governing body will continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments but will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving the men's side unless there is a material change in the circumstances surrounding women's cricket in the country and broader human rights considerations.The decision was approved by the Cricket Scotland Board at a recent meeting of Cricket Scotland Council Limited (CSCL), following an approach by the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) seeking access to training facilities in Scotland.“Cricket Scotland will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving Afghanistan Men unless there is a material change in the circumstances surrounding Afghanistan women's cricket and wider human rights considerations,” the governing body said in its statement.Why Scotland has taken a stand against Afghanistan cricketCricket Scotland said its decision was guided by its strategic commitment to expanding women's and girls' participation in the sport, alongside concerns about the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan.Women's sport has effectively disappeared in the country since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. Women and girls have also faced severe restrictions on education and employment opportunities.One of Cricket Scotland's four strategic priorities is the advancement and growth of women's and girls' cricket. Its board considered the treatment of women and girls, the country's humanitarian situation, its commitment to equality, consultation with the government and the positions taken by other major cricket governing bodies.The move follows similar decisions by Cricket Australia and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), which have suspended bilateral cricketing engagement with Afghanistan over concerns about women's rights.The Taliban government maintains that it respects women's rights in accordance with its interpretation of Islamic law and local customs, and that internal matters should be addressed locally.ICC matches allowed, but training facilities deniedCricket Scotland has clarified that its policy does not extend to ICC tournaments, where fixtures will be determined by competition regulations.“Cricket Scotland will continue to participate in any fixtures against Afghanistan Men at ICC events which are determined by ICC competition regulations,” its statement said.However, the governing body will not host or participate in pre-tour training camps, practice matches or warm-up fixtures involving Afghanistan outside ICC events.The ACB approached Cricket Scotland in July seeking training facilities ahead of the men's series against Ireland. A second request was made in September in connection with the Afghanistan Premier League (APL). The July request was declined due to operational restrictions and to allow the board to consider its position.On franchise cricket, Cricket Scotland said it would honour its contractual obligations to players and issue no-objection certificates (NOCs) if the ICC grants the Afghan league official approval.“If an NOC is issued, participation by that player/s must not be interpreted as an endorsement by Cricket Scotland of the current Afghan regime or its policies,” the statement said.The policy will be reviewed annually or following any significant ICC decision or material change in circumstances.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England Lions hit their highest List A cricket score of 487-5 as Durham's Ben McKinney smashes 145 from 65 balls
articles.summary: Durham opener Ben McKinney smashes 15 fours and 10 sixes in his eye-catching century as England Lions make it five wins from five on West Indies tour; James Rew also scores a ton as Lions eclipse the Ben Duckett-inspired 425-1 the Lions amassed against Sri Lanka A in Canterbury in 2016
articles.body:
The total, in which Durham opener Ben McKinney looted 145 from 65 deliveries - reaching his century from just 43 balls - and James Rew scored 107 not out from 56, eclipsed the 425-1 the Lions racked up against Sri Lanka A at Canterbury a decade ago.

In that match, current England Test and ODI opener Ben Duckett plundered 220 not out from 131 balls and Kent's Daniel Bell-Drummond 171 from 139 after Dawid Malan had fallen for 23.

Ten years on, McKinney and Rew were the stars, with the former smoking 15 fours and 10 sixes and the latter - who made his Test debut against New Zealand at The Kia Oval in June, keeping wicket with Jamie Smith on paternity leave - struck 15 fours and two sixes.

McKinney was linked with a Test call-up earlier this summer when it became clear that England were going to drop Zak Crawley but the spot as Duckett's partner at the top of the order went to the youngster's Durham team-mate Emilio Gay instead.

McKinney and Rew flogged a bowling attack that included full West Indies international Oshane Thomas - the seamer has played 46 white-ball games for his nation, most recently in February 2024.

Australia-bound Jack takes five-wicket haul for Lions

The Lions won the match by 276 runs after skittling their hosts for 211 in reply in Basseterre, thanks chiefly to a five-wicket haul from Hampshire quick Eddie Jack, who has been included in England's T20I squad to take on Australia later this month.

Glamorgan leg-spinner Mason Crane bagged three wickets.

Earlier on with the bat, Lions captain Dan Lawrence - in England's Test squad for the winter trip to South Africa - chipped in with 76 from 56 deliveries and Hampshire youngster Ben Mayes notched an unbeaten 58 from 46.

The Lions have won all five of their matches on the tour so far, following a 3-0 sweep in the T20 series by taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match one-day international leg.

The remaining 50-over matches are also in St Kitts, on Wednesday, Saturday and next Monday.

Jack, Rew's younger brother Thomas - who made 22 in Monday's run-fest - and James Coles are the uncapped players in the senior England T20 international squad to battle Australia in five matches from November 21, with the opening fixture in Melbourne.

Jack, Thomas Rew and Coles will fly out to Australia after the third unofficial ODI against West Indies A.

articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah, Ravindra Jadeja get little game time as third India A vs New Zealand A unofficial Test ends in draw
articles.summary: Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja did not get the match practice they were hoping for as the third unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A
articles.body: Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja did not get the match practice they were hoping for as the third unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A ended in a draw on Tuesday. The fourth and final day was washed out due to rain.The third day of the match was also lost to rain on Monday. All three matches in the series ended in draws, with neither team able to take the honours.Jaiswal shines with another hundredIndia A had scored 464 for 5, with Yashasvi Jaiswal hitting his second century of the series. Sai Sudharsan, Dhruv Jurel, Tilak Varma and Washington Sundar also scored half-centuries.New Zealand A were 36 without loss at the end of the second day's play.The match was important for India as Bumrah and Jadeja were expected to get some game time after a break.Bumrah last played on October 3, in the Asian Games final against Pakistan in Japan's Aichi-Nagoya. He was rested for the white-ball leg of the New Zealand tour to keep him fresh for the two-Test series, which begins in Wellington on November 19.However, Bumrah got to bowl only six overs in the match and gave away 11 runs. He would have wanted to bowl a few spells and get into rhythm ahead of the Test series, but rain did not allow that.Jadeja, who is expected to play a key role with the bat in overseas conditions, got some time in the middle. He faced 71 balls and scored 25 runs during his stay of one hour and 20 minutes.However, he did not get a chance to bowl as India A bowled only 14 overs in the match.India players head to WellingtonBumrah, Jadeja, Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Sudharsan, Washington and Akash Deep will now travel to Wellington. The senior team will look to make the most of six planned training sessions ahead of the first Test, weather permitting.Jaiswal's two back-to-back centuries were among the biggest positives for India A. Padikkal also impressed with 199 runs in the first unofficial Test. His performance has strengthened his case for the No. 3 spot ahead of Sudharsan, who also scored a few half-centuries in the series.Akash Deep's return to action after a long injury break was another positive. It remains to be seen whether head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Shubman Gill will pick him as the fourth specialist fast bowler, alongside Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna.Akash Deep can also contribute with the bat, which could work in his favour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Michael Clarke: Former Australia captain says fans 'can't trust what's real' regarding sandpaper incident
articles.summary: Former Australia captain Michael Clarke says fans of the national side "can't trust what's real" and has called for the investigation into the 2018 Australia ball-tampering scandal to be reopened.
articles.body:
Former Australia captain Michael Clarke has said fans of the national side "can't trust what's real" and has called for the investigation into the 2018 Australia ball-tampering scandal to be reopened.

Clarke's former international team-mate Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball in the third Test against South Africa.

The incident led to bans for captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and fellow batter Cameron Bancroft, but a Cricket Australia investigation found the national side's bowling attack were unaware of the ball-tampering.

Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg, speaking before Clarke's intervention, said he does not see "any compelling reason" to reopen the investigation.

However Clarke said Australian fans "have not moved on" and that the investigation process needs to be restaged.

"They can't trust what's real. They don't know the truth until this gets reopened and the truth comes out," Clarke told 2DayFM.

"We had the chance in 2018. The truth didn't come out. We had the chance in 2021 when [Bancroft] made those comments. The truth didn't come out.

"Now we've got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on."

Khawaja 100% accurate on ball-tampering - Warner

In a 2021 interview with the Guardian, Bancroft was asked if the bowlers knew and replied: "It's pretty probably self-explanatory."

Shortly after Bancroft's interview, Australia's bowling attack in the contentious 2018 Cape Town Test issued a joint statement saying they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".

Pat Cummins featured in that line-up and Clarke said the current Australia Test captain needed to speak on Khawaja's allegations.

"For me, right now, there's more questions than answers," Clarke added.

"I want to know, firstly, did everyone know? Because certain players have come out and said they didn't. I want to know: did they know or not? That's important information so we can get the truth.

"I can't believe we haven't heard from Pat Cummins yet, the Australian captain. Steve Smith lost his job. If this doesn't happen, Tim Paine never captains Australia. And neither does Pat Cummins.

"Pat Cummins would not have captained a game at this stage if 'sandpapergate' didn't happen because Steve Smith would still be captain."

Smith lost his job as Australia captain after receiving a year-long ban for the sandpaper incident and was replaced by Paine. Cummins then took over the Test captaincy in November 2021.

Greenberg said he had not read Khawaja's autobiography in which his claims are made, but said he hoped to do so and that he had "huge respect" for the former batter giving "his version of events".

"There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others," Greenberg told Sports Entertainment Network.

"I want to be really careful to consider what Usman's actually said, and not respond to the headlines or the subsequent commentary that gets created.

"It's important to attribute his words and not the headlines. It's important to know that back at that time, players were urged to come forward, and they had the opportunity to do so over these past eight years, and that remains the case.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman, and our position hasn't changed on that.

"We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again. I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that."

How an 'absolute fluke' exposed sandpapergate scandal

I haven't thrown anyone under the bus - Khawaja

Whole Australia team knew of sandpaper use - Khawaja

Australia seamer Mitchell Starc has said he is disappointed by Khawaja's allegation that the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper.

The quartet of bowlers in the Cape Town Test - Starc, Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon - remain fixtures in the Australia red-ball side.

Speaking at a season launch event in Sydney, Starc stated he hadn't "really paid much attention" to the media coverage of Khawaja's claims.

"Obviously, there's differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process at the time, since," said Starc.

"I guess I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers - but, where I stand, my opinion hasn't changed, my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021.

"We weren't aware it [sandpaper] was taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town. As far as the book's concerned, I haven't read it and probably won't read it, so that's for Usman to elaborate on.

"It's definitely disappointing that's what we're talking about heading into a really exciting [Australian] summer. Different people felt different ways about it at the time, throughout and certainly through the last eight years.

"I think Trav [Head] said it the other day, that the group has changed a lot. We certainly look forward to what's coming up. We're not in 2018 anymore, are we, so the group at the moment's great."

Khawaja has also said in his book that sandpaper was in use at the second Test at Port Elizabeth, and Clarke said that claim also needed to be investigated.

Starc said that allegation was the "first I was aware of any of that taking place in PE".

Warner, who was banned for a year after the incident, has backed Khawaja's recollections, saying on Monday they were "100% accurate".

Greenberg, who took over as Cricket Australia CEO in March 2025 having previously led the Australian Cricketers' Association (ACA), argued there was always likely to be a lack of consensus about what took place in the series.

"You end up at the same intersection where one person's version of events contradict the others, and I'm not sure what outcome people are searching for," he added.

"I think what people want is a single outcome that everyone is aligned up on, but I don't think that's possible on this occasion because we have such conflicting views from the same moment in time."

ACA said in a statement , external the 2018 tour was a "low point for Australian cricket" and the banned players had paid an "enormous" and "disproportionate" price.

They stated that after eight years those involved "may have different recollections and perspectives" and "they are entitled to share their experiences, just as others are entitled to put such a challenging period in their life behind them".

The statement added: "There are no winners in this issue, and nothing can undo what happened. There are humans in the centre of this and we will be calling for the ongoing vitriol directed at those involved to come to an end."

articles.title: ‘It's a wee bit of frustration’: Kyle Jamieson flags New Zealand’s injury-hit bowling attack against India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Zealand pacer Kyle Jamieson has admitted that the hosts' inability to field a settled bowling attack has been a source of frustration
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Zealand pacer Kyle Jamieson has admitted that the hosts' inability to field a settled bowling attack has been a source of frustration during the ongoing white-ball series against India, with injuries disrupting their plans and affecting the team's ability to build consistency.New Zealand lost the five-match T20I series 2-3 and are trailing 0-2 in the five-match ODI series, with the third match abandoned due to inclement weather. The hosts have been without senior pacers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson, while Blair Tickner also suffered an injury during the second ODI.Jamieson believes the repeated changes to the bowling combination have prevented the attack from developing the cohesion needed to challenge India consistently.“It's a wee bit of frustration, right? You're trying to always put a similar attack out and you sort of can build that camaraderie and build that cohesion. We haven't had the reps (repetitions) that we'd like. But hopefully over the next couple of weeks we'll sort of all come out here together and get a good run of cricket together,” Jamieson was quoted as saying by the host broadcasters before the toss in the third ODI.Injuries disrupt New Zealand's bowling plansThe absence of Henry and Ferguson has deprived New Zealand of two experienced fast-bowling options, while Tickner's injury has further complicated their plans. The lack of continuity has been particularly challenging against an Indian batting line-up that has capitalised on the hosts' bowling changes.Jamieson, however, has been among the more effective performers for New Zealand. He troubled India's batters with seam movement and bounce in Wellington, claiming three wickets in the rain-affected contest.“Just trying to manage a little bit of the weather stuff. Trying to get it right on what conditions are going to look like and just trying to put them (opposition) under a little bit of pressure,” he said.Jamieson enjoys conditions offering help to bowlersThe tall pacer also welcomed the conditions in the series, which have offered assistance to the bowlers, contrasting them with batting-friendly surfaces where restricting the opposition to a run rate below 10 is considered a good effort.“No, I love it. I'm so used to like these wickets that are, you know, if you go under tens, you're having a good day. So it's nice to have a little bit in your favour. You can kind of just try and land on a spot and hope you get a little bit of assistance. So, it's nice to have a little bit more in our favour. And long may that continue,” he said.With a demanding run of Test cricket ahead, Jamieson also spoke about the adjustment required when switching from white-ball cricket to the longer format.“It takes a while but just trying to trust the work that you've done, trust the process around it and then just ultimately just sort of surrender into the game, into what may or may not happen,” he said.The pacer added that managing his physical condition had been a major focus during his time away from the game.“I kind of always felt like my game was in an okay space. It was just trying to get the physical and the body side of it sort of, a bit more under my control. I felt like if I could kind of put some of those steps in place, get a run of cricket under my belt, it was always going to be all right,” Jamieson said.“So thankfully I sort of feel like I'm coming out the other side of it now and obviously a big run of Test cricket coming up. So touch wood we survive that,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Sandpapergate': Mitchell Starc denies knowledge after Usman Khawaja claims as Cricket Australia says investigation will not be re-opened
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja claims in new book 'Sabr' that every Australia player was aware of ball-tampering scheme in Cape Town in 2018; current Test captain Pat Cummins set to speak to media in coming days and weeks; Mitchell Starc says recollections have not changed as he denies knowledge of plot
articles.body:
Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', bringing the scandal back onto the agenda after eight years.

David Warner - who said on Monday that Khawaja's version of events was "100 per cent accurate" - then captain Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were banned after the sandpaper affair, with Cricket Australia asserting only that trio were privy to the plot to alter the condition of the ball in order to try and make it swing.

The bowlers in that Cape Town Test - seamers Starc, Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon - released a joint statement in 2021 saying they were not aware of the tampering.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, after Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg insisted there would be no re-opening of the 'Sandpapergate' investigation , Starc said of Khawaja's claims: "I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair.

"There are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process, at the time and since.

"I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers but from where I stand my opinion hasn't changed, my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021.

"As far as our statement said, we weren't aware of things being taken on the field. That's where I'll leave it.

"I will be sticking to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time eight years ago, so clearly there is differing versions from different people.

"We weren't aware of anything taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town.

"As far as the book is concerned, I haven't read it. I probably won't read it, so that's for Usman to elaborate on."

On Khawaja saying the ball was also tampered with in the Test before the Cape Town fixture, at Port Elizabeth, now Gqeberha, Starc added: "That's the first I was aware of any of that."

Healy: Timing of Khawaja comments 'a little bit sticky'

Starc's wife, former Australia captain Alyssa Healy, addressed the fallout on the Keepin' it Cricket podcast after Khawaja insisted he had not "thrown anyone under the bus", with the 36-year-old calling the timing of his comments "sticky".

Healy said: "Been scraping off bits of Mitch off the bitumen after the bus had just hit him over the last two days.

"I'm obviously in quite a unique predicament: I'm working in the media, I have to comment on these things [and] I'm also married to one of the players who is still playing who was there in that series and experienced all of that eight years ago.

"It's a hard one for me to comment on. I'm kind of going to sit back and watch it unfold I think, first and foremost, but what I will say is that the timing of it is just a little bit sticky for me. I don't like that."

A statement from the Australian Cricketers' Association called the 2018 scandal a "low point for Australian cricket" for which Smith, Warner and Bancroft paid an "enormous" and "disproportionate" price.

The statement added: "There are no winners in this issue, and nothing can undo what happened. There are humans in the centre of this and we will be calling for the ongoing vitriol directed at those involved to come to an end."

Cricket Australia: No compelling reason to re-open 'Sandpapergate' case

Current Test captain Cummins is poised to speak about the issue publicly in the coming days or weeks, according to Greenberg.

Greenberg, who was not part of Cricket Australia at the time of the scandal, told Australian radio station SEN on the decision not to launch a fresh inquiry: "We don't see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again.

"I don't think there's anything that can be gained from that.

"We have said we're comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we've received. That includes what we've seen from Usman. Our position hasn't changed on that.

"There's absolutely no benefit in going back, that's the clear position of the CA board. I think it's fine, we've got to look ahead, and the matter was dealt with under a previous leadership back in 2018.

"Trying to second-guess decisions from a previous time or making an assessment through the prism of hindsight is not something we want to do."

'Usman's version of events inconsistent with what others say'

Greenberg added: "When you cut to the core of the challenge that we face here, Usman's version of events is inconsistent with what others have had to say.

"I can assure you there are lots of other players who have a very, very different version of events and they have made that very public from the very start of 2018.

"They have been very consistent in their position right through until today. From my conversations with many over the weekend, I don't think that will change either.

"I think we end up at the same intersection point, which is eight years ago people have a version of events which differ from each other.

"No one would like to get this chapter of Australian cricket closed more than me, but it is unlikely."

Cummins, Starc, Lyon and Hazlewood are not part of the upcoming white-ball series at home to England.

However, batting all-rounder Mitchell Marsh, who also played in the 'Sandpapergate' Test, will captain the side in the three ODIs and five T20s.

Marsh is due to give a press conference on Thursday ahead of the first ODI at Perth's Optus Stadium the following day.

Former Australia captain Michael Clarke hopes the truth comes to light, saying that chance was missed in the wake of the scandal in 2018 and then again three years later when Bancroft replied it was "probably self-explanatory" after being asked whether the bowling attack knew of the sandpaper use.

Clarke told 2DayFM : "[Australia fans] can't trust what's real. They don't know the truth until this gets reopened and the truth comes out. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to move on.

"For me, right now, there's more questions than answers. I want to know, firstly, did everyone know? Because certain players have come out and said they didn't. That's important information so we can get the truth.

"I can't believe we haven't heard from Cummins yet. Steve Smith lost his job. If this doesn't happen, Tim Paine never captains Australia. And neither does Cummins.

"Cummins would not have captained a game at this stage if 'Sandpapergate' didn't happen because Smith would still be captain."

articles.title: India vs New Zealand: How weather spoilt families' day out in Hamilton
articles.summary: HAMILTON: Around 2:30 PM local time, 30 minutes before the official start time for the third ODI, the Indian team bus arrived at the Seddon Park in
articles.body: HAMILTON: Around 2:30 PM local time, 30 minutes before the official start time for the third ODI, the Indian team bus arrived at the Seddon Park in Hamilton. When the doors opened, the assembled Indian fans were in for a surprise. With their phones pointed to the bus, expecting the entire squad to emerge, the first, and only, player to emerge for a discussion with the local and India's operations teams was former India captain Rohit Sharma. After a long chat, Rohit sprinted to the stadium and did not return for close to 15 minutes.With the door closed, the players continued to sit inside waiting for the go-ahead from the team management. Rohit finally returned to the bus amid loud chants but none of the players got down as another discussion ensued. It was later learnt that if the players had entered the Players and Match Officials Area (PMOA), they wouldn't have been allowed to exit and re-enter as per the guidelines. So a decision to return to the team hotel was taken as drizzle continued and the ground remained far from ready.Before the team bus could get going for the Indian team hotel, having waited for over half-an-hour, captain Shubman Gill, coach Gautam Gambhir and other support staff members joined New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner. The rest of the BlackCaps players who had arrived by their own cars, also waited outside the venue. When they didn't get the necessary go-ahead, they also began driving back to the team hotel.When the weather finally cleared and the outfield was prepared in lightning-quick time, the Indian team bus returned. Meanwhile, Rohit beat the pack as he travelled with New Zealand players in their car.It was a frustrating day of waiting, rain and chilly winds in Hamilton, and even more so for the numerous family members gathered in the hospitality box.From Rohit Sharma's wife Ritika to Shubman Gill and Arshdeep Singh's parents, all had taken their seats when the toss and revised timings were announced. Gill won another flip of the coin, and just when the Indian players started warming-up to get ready for action, another drizzle sent them off the field, never to return.Rohit would occasionally emerge from the dressing room to wave to his daughter in the stands and gestured to Gill Sr but even that didn't last long as the rain got heavier, forcing the players indoors and leaving match officials with the formal announcement to abandon the contest. When it was announced on the PA, the fans quickly rushed out to position themselves near the team bus, for the third time that day, and another surprise was in store.Virat Kohli, amid loud chants of "Radhe! Radhe!", left in a private car with Gill, Ishan Kishan and Naman Dhir. Even Rohit ditched the team bus and left in a car while the rest, featuring Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, coach Gambhir, boarded the team bus to end the long day of waiting and rain.For the fans, it was an afternoon spent soaking in the rain to catch a glimpse of their favourite cricketers and the maximum they got was a 10-second glimpse of the players entering and exiting their respective vehicles.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaryavir Sehwag joins Shubman Gill, Mayank Agarwal in elite list with stunning 160 against UAE
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Aaryavir Sehwag produced a sensational innings of 160 to join India captain Shubman Gill and Mayank Agarwal in an elite list of Indian batters
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Aaryavir Sehwag produced a sensational innings of 160 to join India captain Shubman Gill and Mayank Agarwal in an elite list of Indian batters during the ACC U19 Asia Cup clash against the United Arab Emirates at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman on Tuesday.The right-hander struck 17 fours and seven sixes in his 168-ball knock, registering the joint fifth-highest individual score by an Indian batter in Youth ODIs. His effort also matched the 160s scored by Gill and Agarwal at the Under-19 level.Gill had scored 160 against England at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium in 2017, while Agarwal reached the same score against Australia in Hobart in 2009.Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, also shared a massive 193-run partnership for the second wicket with VK Vineeth, putting India in a commanding position after UAE won the toss and elected to field.Sehwag falls short of Rayudu's long-standing recordSehwag looked set to challenge the long-standing record for the highest individual score by an Indian in Youth ODIs, but his marathon innings came to an end in the 45th over.He was dismissed for 160 off 168 balls, caught by Uddish Suri at mid-wicket off Naseem Khan in the 45th over. Attempting to pull a slower short-of-length delivery across the line, Sehwag failed to get the required timing and found the fielder.The record remains with Ambati Rayudu, who scored an unbeaten 177 against England U19 in Taunton in 2002.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi came close to breaking that mark earlier in 2026, smashing 175 off just 80 balls against England in the Under-19 World Cup final. Sooryavanshi also occupies the third position on the list with his 171 against UAE in 2025.Raj Bawa's unbeaten 162 against Uganda in 2022 is the fourth-highest score by an Indian in Youth ODIs.Sehwag's 160 puts him alongside Gill and Agarwal in the next position on the list.From cautious start to a boundary-filled assaultSehwag began his innings cautiously as India reached 42 without loss in the first 10 overs. However, once settled, he shifted gears and took on the UAE bowling attack, combining boundaries with smart running between the wickets.His partnership with Vineeth proved crucial in rebuilding and accelerating India's innings after the opening stand. The 193-run second-wicket association gave India the platform to push for a substantial total.India had entered the contest looking to bounce back after their three-wicket defeat to Pakistan in their previous group match. Despite Arjun Rajput's century, India were bowled out for 208 before Pakistan chased down the target, powered by Hamza Zahoor's match-winning hundred.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Australian fans have not moved on’: Michael Clarke joins Sandpapergate storm as pressure mounts on Cricket Australia
articles.summary: The controversy surrounding Australia's 2018 Sandpapergate scandal has taken another turn, with former captain Michael Clarke joining the growing chorus
articles.body: The controversy surrounding Australia's 2018 Sandpapergate scandal has taken another turn, with former captain Michael Clarke joining the growing chorus demanding that Cricket Australia (CA) reopen its investigation following Usman Khawaja's explosive revelations.Clarke believes Australian cricket fans have still not received the complete truth about the ball-tampering episode and said the issue would continue to haunt the game until the investigation was revisited. His comments come amid contrasting accounts from former teammates, with David Warner backing Khawaja's version, Mitchell Starc standing by the bowlers' earlier statement and CA chief executive Todd Greenberg ruling out another probe.“We haven’t moved on. Australian fans have not moved on. They can’t trust what’s real. They don’t know the truth – until this (investigation) gets reopened and the truth comes out,” Clarke said on 2DayFM’s Breakfast with Nath & Emma.Clarke wants the complete truth to emergeKhawaja reignited the debate through his forthcoming autobiography, Sabr, claiming that the entire Australian Test dressing room, including players and support staff, knew about the use of sandpaper during the 2018 tour of South Africa.The controversy first erupted during the third Test at Cape Town, where Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball. Smith, Warner and Bancroft subsequently received suspensions, with the latter two also facing additional sanctions.Clarke said the opportunity to establish the complete truth had been missed in 2018 and again when Bancroft made comments about the involvement of other players in a 2021 interview with The Guardian.“We had the chance in 2018. The truth didn’t come out. We had the chance in 2021 when (Cameron Bancroft) made those comments (to The Guardian). The truth didn’t come out. Now we’ve got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on,” he said.Clarke also raised questions about whether the alleged ball-tampering had started before the Cape Town Test, as claimed by Khawaja.“For me, right now, there’s more questions than answers. I want to know, firstly, did everyone know? Because certain players have come out and said they didn’t. I want to know: did they know or not? That’s important information so we can get the truth. And did it happen in the game before? That’s also what I’m hearing, that (it didn’t just happen) in Cape Town,” Clarke added.Starc stands by bowlers as Warner backs KhawajaThe latest developments have exposed sharply contrasting positions among members of the Australian side involved in the scandal.Warner, who received a 12-month ban for his role in the episode, publicly backed Khawaja, describing his account as “100% accurate”. He also criticised CA's original investigation as “botched” and “rushed”.Starc, meanwhile, reiterated that his recollection had not changed from the position outlined in the joint statement issued by Australia's four frontline bowlers in 2021.“I haven’t really paid much attention to be fair, obviously there’s differing opinions of eight years ago,” Starc told reporters in Sydney.“We were heavily drilled through the process at the time, and since and I guess I won’t speak on behalf of the bowlers, but where I stand, my opinion hasn’t changed. My recollection hasn’t changed from what we said in 2021.”The statement had been issued by Starc, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon after Bancroft's 2021 interview raised questions about how much the bowling group knew. The quartet denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball.Starc also said Khawaja's claim that sandpaper had been used during the second Test in Gqeberha was news to him.“I'll leave said authors to explain,” he said.Cricket Australia refuses to reopen investigationDespite the renewed calls for answers, Greenberg has ruled out reopening the investigation, saying CA remains satisfied with the original findings.“There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others,” Greenberg said.“But we have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received.”He added: “That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that.”Meanwhile, Khawaja responded on social media to suggestions that his revelations were intended to boost sales of his autobiography.“I'm very fortunate, I don't need the money,” he said.With Clarke now joining Warner in questioning the original investigation, and Starc maintaining the bowlers' position, the Sandpapergate controversy continues to divide Australian cricket nearly eight years after the incident.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No doubt I will be back': Marnus Labuschagne unfazed by Test omission, backs himself to reclaim Australia spot
articles.summary: Marnus Labuschagne is refusing to let his latest Test setback dent his confidence, insisting he has no doubt about returning to the Australian side after
articles.body: Marnus Labuschagne is refusing to let his latest Test setback dent his confidence, insisting he has no doubt about returning to the Australian side after being dropped for the upcoming World Test Championship series against New Zealand. The 32-year-old, however, is ready to put the scrutiny behind him for now, shifting his focus to domestic cricket and helping Queensland win games in the Sheffield Shield.Labuschagne's omission comes after a prolonged lean patch in Test cricket, with the right-hander struggling to rediscover the consistency that once made him one of Australia's most dependable batters. Despite the disappointment, he believes a return to domestic cricket will give him the opportunity to regain his rhythm and put himself back in contention for national selection.Speaking at the Gabba ahead of Queensland's Sheffield Shield clash, Labuschagne acknowledged the pressure he has been under over the past couple of years and said he intends to use this period to enjoy his cricket again."You are pretty aware as a cricketer ... you use this as an opportunity to step back from the scrutiny, and being under the pump for probably two years now,” Labuschagne told the media on Tuesday, as quoted by Fox Sports.“You take this opportunity to come back and play for Queensland, enjoy your time here and find ways to win games for Queensland. Score runs, enjoy the games and I think my path back to the Australian team will work itself out."'No doubt I will be back': Labuschagne backs himself for Australia returnThe Australian batter has experienced a similar setback before. He was left out of the squad for Australia's tour of the West Indies last year but responded emphatically, scoring five centuries across red-ball and white-ball cricket for Queensland in eight innings to force his way back into the national setup ahead of the home Ashes series against England.Drawing confidence from that experience, Labuschagne remains optimistic about earning another opportunity, although he admitted that he does not know when the recall could come."I have done it before, and I have got no doubt I will be back there. When? Who knows, but that is the aspiration and desire. Right now, my feet are firmly fixed here with Queensland and doing whatever I can as a captain, batter, in the field and with the ball to help us win games," he added.Labuschagne names potential contenders for Australia's No. 3 spotWith Labuschagne out of the picture for the New Zealand assignment, the competition for Australia's No. 3 position is expected to intensify. Asked about the possible candidates who could fill the vacancy, the Queensland captain highlighted Jack Clayton, Kurtis Patterson and Sam Konstas among the available options.Clayton, in particular, has impressed with his recent performances in the Sheffield Shield, and Labuschagne was quick to praise his batting form while offering his support as the youngster navigates the possibility of stepping into the international spotlight."There are some candidates; the likes of Jack Clayton has scored some runs in the last two Shield games, and is batting beautifully. Sam Konstas scored some runs, there’s a lot of good batters around the country, Kurtis Patterson has scored some runs in the last few years (too)," he said."It is not for me to work out. I think there is options there, and they have also got some internal options in the way they can re-jig the order. My thing for Jack is I am here to support him, and I understand this is the first time for him on this journey of being in the spotlight. Whatever I can do to help him and make him feel comfortable ... he is a fabulous player and a really good kid," he added.Labuschagne's prolonged Test batting slump behind omissionLabuschagne's exclusion follows a difficult run of form in the longest format. He managed just 131 runs across six innings during Australia's recent three-Test series against South Africa, further strengthening the selectors' case for a change ahead of the crucial WTC assignment against New Zealand.His struggles have extended well beyond that series. Since scoring his last Test century against England at Old Trafford in July 2023, Labuschagne has gone 26 Tests and 49 innings without reaching three figures.During that period, he has accumulated 1,094 runs at an average of 24.31, including nine half-centuries. The numbers represent a significant fall from the standards he established earlier in his Test career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fresh Sandpapergate storm puts Mitchell Starc in spotlight; Alyssa Healy reveals her stance: 'Slightly conflicted'
articles.summary: The infamous Sandpapergate scandal has returned to haunt Australian cricket, with fresh claims from former batter Usman Khawaja reigniting debate over the
articles.body: The infamous Sandpapergate scandal has returned to haunt Australian cricket, with fresh claims from former batter Usman Khawaja reigniting debate over the 2018 ball-tampering controversy. This time, the spotlight has fallen on Mitchell Starc, with his wife and former Australia women's captain Alyssa Healy admitting that she feels "slightly conflicted" about the renewed allegations.Khawaja, in his newly released autobiography Sabr, made explosive revelations about the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, claiming that the entire Australian Test team was aware of the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball. He also alleged that ball-tampering was not restricted to the infamous third Test, with the practice reportedly taking place during the second Test of the series as well.Starc, however, has firmly rejected Khawaja's claims, maintaining that he stands by the joint statement released in 2021 alongside Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four Australian fast bowlers had denied knowing about the sandpaper being taken onto the field and the ball being tampered with during the Cape Town Test.Alyssa Healy reacts to fresh Sandpapergate allegations involving Mitchell StarcSpeaking at Kayo Sports and Fox Cricket's launch event, Healy admitted that the situation was difficult for her to comment on, given her personal connection to the controversy."It's a hard one to comment on. At the moment, I feel slightly conflicted, and I'm in the middle of it. It's hard to make a comment on it, we'll see where it goes and if CA do take it forward or how it rolls throughout the media, and I'll make a comment from there. For now, I'm just gonna sit and wait and watch it unfold," Healy said.Her comments come after Starc publicly pushed back against Khawaja's version of events, insisting that his position on the controversy remains unchanged.What is the Sandpapergate controversy? The Sandpapergate scandal dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa at Newlands, Cape Town, in March 2018. During the match, television cameras captured Cameron Bancroft using a piece of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball.The incident triggered one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket history. Bancroft was handed a nine-month suspension, while then-captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner received 12-month bans from international and domestic cricket. Smith was also removed from the captaincy, while Warner was banned from holding a leadership position in Australian cricket.Khawaja's latest revelations have brought the episode back into the spotlight, with questions being raised about how widespread the knowledge of the ball-tampering operation was within the Australian dressing room.However, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has indicated that the governing body has little interest in reopening the matter more than eight years after the incident. Healy backed that approach, suggesting that Australian cricket should focus on moving forward rather than revisiting a controversy that had already left a lasting impact on those involved."I watched it eight years ago too. I think the game of cricket as a whole has moved on. (Cricket Australia CEO) Todd Greenberg's statement today about not looking into it any further is a great sign of where we're headed and that's moving forward and looking ahead to this summer," she said.Healy urges empathy for those involved in SandpapergateShe said the individuals mentioned in Khawaja's book were being forced to revisit difficult memories and urged people to consider the emotional toll of the renewed scrutiny."I feel for everyone involved. I know a human element in it as well that people are being dragged back through some things and reliving some memories. I think from a human side of things we've got to remember that and put our arms around the people that are being mentioned," she added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Debutants Tayyab Arif, Arafat Minhas shine as Pakistan pile up 434 before reducing Sri Lanka to 114/3 in Rawalpindi Test
articles.summary: Pakistan strengthened their position in the opening Test against Sri Lanka with a commanding batting display on Day 2 in Rawalpindi, posting 434/9 before
articles.body: Pakistan strengthened their position in the opening Test against Sri Lanka with a commanding batting display on Day 2 in Rawalpindi, posting 434/9 before reducing the visitors to 114/3 at stumps. Saud Shakeel narrowly missed a century, while debutants Tayyab Arif and Arafat Minhas made valuable half-centuries to put the hosts in control of the contest.Pakistan resumed the day at 281/5 and added 153 runs before captain Babar Azam declared the innings at 434/9 in 106.3 overs. Sri Lanka, who had opted to bowl after winning the toss, struggled to make early inroads as Pakistan's middle and lower order continued to frustrate their bowling attack.The visitors lost three wickets in their reply, with Mohammad Abbas and debutant Saqib Khan making crucial breakthroughs. Sri Lanka finished the day at 114/3, trailing Pakistan by 320 runs, with Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva unbeaten when bad light brought an early end to proceedings.Saud Shakeel misses century as Pakistan build commanding totalResuming on 57, Saud Shakeel continued his patient knock and combined with wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi Ghori to frustrate the Sri Lankan bowlers. The duo stitched together a valuable 96-run partnership for the sixth wicket, taking Pakistan past the 300-run mark. Ghori looked set for a maiden Test half-century but fell for 48 off 72 deliveries after edging Dilshan Madushanka to Pasindu Sooriyabandara at gully. His innings included two boundaries and provided Pakistan with an important contribution in the morning session.Shakeel continued to hold one end together and moved closer to his fifth Test century. However, Asitha Fernando ended his resistance at 93 off 199 balls, with nine boundaries, as Kusal Mendis completed the catch.The dismissal also gave Fernando his 100th Test wicket, marking a significant milestone for the Sri Lankan pacer.Debutants Tayyab Arif, Arafat Minhas shine as Pakistan declare at 434/9Pakistan's batting effort was supported by some impressive contributions from their debutants. Tayyab Arif had earlier scored a quickfire 57 off 51 balls, while Arafat Minhas continued his promising start to international cricket with a half-century.Minhas scored 52 off 72 deliveries, striking nine boundaries and a six. His counter-attacking approach helped Pakistan maintain the momentum even after the departure of Shakeel. Mohammad Taha also contributed a valuable 51, while captain Babar Azam scored 50 off 58 balls. The duo's half-centuries ensured Pakistan had contributions throughout the batting order.After Lahiru Kumara dismissed Razaullah for 10, Pakistan declared their first innings at 434/9 in 106.3 overs.For Sri Lanka, Asitha Fernando and Dilshan Madushanka picked up three wickets apiece, while Lahiru Kumara, Milan Rathnayake and Sonal Dinusha claimed one wicket each.Mohammad Abbas, Saqib Khan strike as Sri Lanka lose three wicketsChasing Pakistan's first-innings total, Sri Lanka endured a difficult start as Mohammad Abbas struck early to remove Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck. Debutant Saqib Khan then made an immediate impact, dismissing Dinesh Chandimal for just one run to leave the visitors struggling at 12/2.Lahiru Udara attempted to stabilise the innings and played some positive strokes, scoring 42 off 52 deliveries with seven boundaries. However, Saqib returned to dismiss him, with Ghazi Ghori completing the catch behind the stumps.Sri Lanka slipped to 65/3, handing Pakistan a significant advantage in the contest.Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva offer resistance before bad light stops playWith three wickets down, Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva took responsibility for rebuilding the Sri Lankan innings.The pair showed composure against Pakistan's bowling attack and put together an unbeaten 49-run partnership to prevent further damage before the close of play. Mendis remained unbeaten on 40 off 78 deliveries, while de Silva was batting on 22 off 28 balls. Their partnership helped Sri Lanka reach 114/3 in 27.1 overs.However, bad light forced the players off the field, bringing Day 2 to an early conclusion.Sri Lanka still trail Pakistan by 320 runs, with seven first-innings wickets remaining. The visitors will need a substantial partnership on Day 3 to reduce the deficit and prevent Pakistan from taking complete control of the opening Test.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Scotland suspended cricket ties with Afghanistan outside ICC events
articles.summary: Cricket Scotland has decided to halt all cricket-related activities with Afghanistan, excluding ICC events, driven by serious concerns regarding the Taliban'...
articles.body:
Cricket Scotland has decided to suspend cricketing engagement with Afghanistan outside International Cricket Council (ICC) events, citing the Taliban government's treatment of women and girls and wider human rights concerns. The governing body will continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments but will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving the men's side unless there is a material change in the circumstances surrounding women's cricket in the country and broader human rights considerations. The decision was approved by the Cricket Scotland Board at a recent meeting of Cricket Scotland Council Limited (CSCL), following an approach by the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) seeking access to training facilities in Scotland. "Cricket Scotland will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving Afghanistan Men unless there is a material change in the circumstances surrounding Afghanistan women's cricket and wider human rights considerations," the governing body said in its statement.

Why Scotland has taken a stand against Afghanistan cricket

Cricket Scotland said its decision was guided by its strategic commitment to expanding women's and girls' participation in the sport, alongside concerns about the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan. Women's sport has effectively disappeared in the country since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. Women and girls have also faced severe restrictions on education and employment opportunities. One of Cricket Scotland's four strategic priorities is the advancement and growth of women's and girls' cricket. Its board considered the treatment of women and girls, the country's humanitarian situation, its commitment to equality, consultation with the government and the positions taken by other major cricket governing bodies. The move follows similar decisions by Cricket Australia and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), which have suspended bilateral cricketing engagement with Afghanistan over concerns about women's rights. The Taliban government maintains that it respects women's rights in accordance with its interpretation of Islamic law and local customs, and that internal matters should be addressed locally.

ICC matches allowed, but training facilities denied

Cricket Scotland has clarified that its policy does not extend to ICC tournaments, where fixtures will be determined by competition regulations. "Cricket Scotland will continue to participate in any fixtures against Afghanistan Men at ICC events which are determined by ICC competition regulations," its statement said. However, the governing body will not host or participate in pre-tour training camps, practice matches or warm-up fixtures involving Afghanistan outside ICC events. The ACB approached Cricket Scotland in July seeking training facilities ahead of the men's series against Ireland. A second request was made in September in connection with the Afghanistan Premier League (APL). The July request was declined due to operational restrictions and to allow the board to consider its position. On franchise cricket, Cricket Scotland said it would honour its contractual obligations to players and issue no-objection certificates (NOCs) if the ICC grants the Afghan league official approval. "If an NOC is issued, participation by that player/s must not be interpreted as an endorsement by Cricket Scotland of the current Afghan regime or its policies," the statement said. The policy will be reviewed annually or following any significant ICC decision or material change in circumstances.

articles.title: Highlights of new Jacksonville Jaguars' S Jessie Bates
articles.summary: Here are some highlights of new Jacksonville Jaguars' safety Jessie Bates from his time in Atlanta.

The first of three Monday trades for the Jacksonville Jaguars was acquiring safety Jessie Bates in a deal with the Atlanta Falcons.

To land Bates, the Jaguars are sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to Atlanta. With the Falcons reportedly taking on the bulk of Bates' remaining 2026 salary, Jacksonville likely had to pay a premium to land the safety.

Bates has been durable during his time with the Falcons and has had very strong ball production over his career, totaling 30 interceptions and 46 pass breakups since entering the NFL in 2018. He is a one-time Pro Bowler and a three-time second-team All-Pro.

Bates will step into a starting safety role with the Jaguars next to Antonio Johnson.

articles.title: Why MI-Hardik Pandya relationship did not work out? Full timeline and factors behind the exit of Mumbai Indians captain
articles.summary: Hardik Pandya has finally ended his second stint with Mumbai Indians and has formally joined Punjab Kings ahead of the IPL 2027 campaign.
articles.body:
Hardik Pandya has left Mumbai Indians to join Punjab Kings ahead of the IPL 2027 campaign.

Pandya re-joined MI from Gujarat Titans in 2024.

Full timeline of factors that led to Pandya's exit from MI.

Hardik Pandya's second stint at MI ends as he joins Punjab Kings

Hardik Pandya's journey as a Mumbai Indians player and captain has finally come to an end as he has formally completed a move to Punjab Kings.

Pandya's move was part of a swap deal that MI agreed to, which will see India fast bowler Arshdeep Singh joining them for the upcoming IPL 2027 campaign.

The experienced all-rounder started his journey in the Indian Premier League with MI in 2015 and spent six seasons during his first stint. It was at MI, where Pandya rose to stardom and also made his international debut for the Men in Blue.

Ahead of the IPL 2022 campaign, Pandya left MI and was picked by the newly formed franchise, Gujarat Titans, at the mega-auction that year and was made the captain of the new side.

In his maiden season with GT, Pandya guided the team to an IPL title and then led them to a second consecutive final in 2023, where they lost to CSK.

After spending only two seasons in Ahmedabad, Pandya returned to MI in a much-hyped move ahead of the IPL 2024 campaign. MI signed Pandya during the trade window and also made his the team captain.

The second stint, however, did not go as per plan, as MI failed to reach the play-offs in two out of the three seasons he led them, and there was also plenty of friction in the dressing room throughout his stint.

Why did the MI-Hardik Pandya relationship not work out? Full timeline and factors behind the exit of Mumbai Indians captain

There were several factors that led to Pandya's exit from MI after just three seasons. Here is a timeline of factors that led to the all-rounder leaving Mumbai for PBKS.

March 2024: Hardik Pandya formally assumes MI captain's role from Rohit Sharma

Soon after Pandya's signing from GT was confirmed, the MI management took a bold call by sacking five-time IPL champion and then-India captain Rohit Sharma from the captain's role and appointing the all-rounder as their new skipper.

The decision instantly sparked anger among fans, especially those who adored Sharma, as the MI management faced severe criticism from a large section ot their supporters.

The video saga: Hardik Pandya praising CSK over MI after joining GT

After Pandya was announced as the next MI captain, a section of the outraged fans dug up old clippings of the all-rounder from his GT days. One such video surfaced online from 2022, where Pandya can be heard praising CSK's team environment, which often leads to their title wins, while, according to him, MI's success is purely on the star players they purchase.

After joining GT, Pandya, in an interview, had said, "There are two kinds of success you can get. One is get the best people possible from A to B which I feel MI had or have the best environment possible for you to win which has been a CSK type where no matter who players are, they find comfort there and best out of them."

April 2024: Fans boo Hardik Pandya at Wankhede Stadium

Things further worsened between Pandya and MI fans as the IPL 2024 campaign kicked off. During a home match of MI at the Wankhede Stadium, the fans famously booed their new captain in an unprecedented event. MI eventually finished at the rock bottom that season with only four wins from 14 matches.

IPL 2026: Hardik Pandya lost MI dressing room as relationship soured with senior stars

After achieving moderate success in 2025, which saw MI reach the Eliminator 2, it seemed the five-time champions were finally getting back to normalcy, and Pandya was finally being accepted as the leader of the pack.

However, things turned ugly again at the start of the 2026 campaign as several media reports surfaced that Pandya had lost the MI dressing and his relationship with senior stars of the team is at its lowest point. By then, the all-rounder was both physically and mentally drained, and it became evident that this was the last season for Pandya at the franchise.

According to Revsportz's Boria Majumder , MI held talks with their captain in June 2026 and then in August and September; the parties had four options in front of them. MI had swap deal offers from KKR, where they were offering Cameron Green and a fast bowler.

RR agreed to trade Yashasvi Jaiswal for Pandya, and the third offer was from Punjab, where they offered Arshdeep, which eventually materialised. A fourth option that MI offered to Pandya was to stay back for one more season before the mega-auction next year.
